heading: Appendix D All 240 story premises
intro: All entries below are **ideas, not completed scripts or rendered catalogue treatments**. Learning claims remain unverified until a claim-level check. Fictional themes are not empirical claims. Each entry retains the authored premise, hook, visible action, intended takeaway and risk. Originality means authored for the catalogue, not an exhaustive prior-art search. The current story-first review may reject or substantially rewrite a premise.

premises.title: The Half-Platform Problem
premises.premise: A conductor must connect two half-length platforms, but differently divided tiles make the lengths look unequal. Sliding both onto the same unit rail reveals equivalent fractions and completes the bridge.
premises.hook: Which platform is actually longer?
premises.visible_action: Fraction tiles slide along a fixed rail; subdivision marks appear without changing either tile length.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Equivalent fractions describe the same amount when the whole stays fixed.
premises.gate: Keep the reference whole identical and verify every tile length.

premises.title: The Basement Delivery
premises.premise: A courier starts two floors below ground and must rise five floors, but treats the ground-floor label as an extra step. A numbered elevator track exposes the counting error and delivers the parcel to floor three.
premises.hook: Five floors up from minus two: where do we land?
premises.visible_action: An elevator advances one tick per beat; a ghost counter incorrectly counts the starting floor.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Movement on a number line counts intervals, not the starting position.
premises.gate: Keep floor numbering explicitly mathematical rather than a real building convention.

premises.title: The Ten-Token Gate
premises.premise: A tally keeper must display thirteen tokens using two slots, but the ones slot accepts only nine. Trading ten ones for one ten opens the gate and leaves three ones.
premises.hook: This slot is full, but three tokens still need counting.
premises.visible_action: Ten unit blocks snap into a transparent ten-block bar; the bar moves into the tens column.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Place value groups quantities in powers of the chosen base.
premises.gate: State base ten and distinguish an empty slot from a missing digit.

premises.title: Same Fence, Different Garden
premises.premise: Two gardeners each receive twelve fence segments and want the largest rectangular planting area. Their first rectangles enclose different tile counts; rearranging the same segments reveals why equal perimeters need not give equal areas.
premises.hook: They have the same fence. Do they get the same garden?
premises.visible_action: Twelve boundary sticks hinge into one-by-five and three-by-three rectangles as unit squares fill the interiors.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Perimeter measures a boundary; area measures the enclosed surface.
premises.gate: Use unit-width fences with explicitly labeled idealized dimensions.

premises.title: The Bag That Refuses a Promise
premises.premise: A host wants to predict the next color from a bag with three blue tokens and one orange token, but a surprising orange draw ruins a confident announcement. A probability label replaces the promise.
premises.hook: Three blues and one orange: can orange still win?
premises.visible_action: Four tokens enter an opaque bag; possible outcomes fan into equal-sized branches before one is selected.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A more likely outcome is not a guaranteed outcome.
premises.gate: Specify equal selection chances and whether each draw replaces the token.

premises.title: The Fair-Share Seesaw
premises.premise: Three islanders want an equal pile of stones, but their piles contain two, four, and nine. A transfer machine redistributes the fifteen stones into three piles of five and balances their platform.
premises.hook: What number can stand in for all three piles?
premises.visible_action: Single stones move between labeled piles; a running total stays fixed while a seesaw levels.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: The arithmetic mean is the total divided by the number of values.
premises.gate: Show that the mean need not match an original value; avoid calling it universally representative.

premises.title: The Purple-Paint Conveyor
premises.premise: A mural robot must preserve a two-to-three blue-red mixing recipe while making a larger batch, but adding the same number to both ingredients changes the recipe. Doubling both counts restores the intended ratio.
premises.hook: Will two extra scoops keep this purple the same?
premises.visible_action: Blue and red counters pair into recipe bundles; unmatched counters flash when an additive shortcut is tried.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Scaling a ratio multiplies every part by the same factor.
premises.gate: Use symbolic color counters; real pigment mixing is not modeled.

premises.title: The Giant Three-Point Jump
premises.premise: An announcer wants an honest chart of scores 97 and 100, but a cropped vertical axis makes the change look enormous. Restoring a labeled zero baseline and displaying the difference lets the audience compare both views.
premises.hook: Did the score triple, or did the camera move?
premises.visible_action: A bar-chart camera pulls back to expose the hidden axis range while numeric labels remain fixed.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Chart scale can change visual emphasis without changing the numbers.
premises.gate: Explain that a nonzero axis is not automatically dishonest; context and labeling matter.

premises.title: The Mirror-Tile Repair
premises.premise: A mosaic maker must repair a reflected pattern, but copies a tile to the same side of the mirror line. Folding the drawing makes paired positions touch and reveals the missing tile location.
premises.hook: Where would this tile land if the page folded?
premises.visible_action: A dashed axis becomes a hinge; square tiles reflect across it along perpendicular guide tracks.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Reflection preserves distance to the mirror line on the opposite side.
premises.gate: Use an explicit reflection axis and avoid confusing reflection with rotation.

premises.title: The Unpaired Umbrella
premises.premise: A coat-check robot must place seventeen umbrellas into groups of four, but keeps waiting for a fifth full group. Four groups fill, one umbrella remains, and a remainder shelf completes the count honestly.
premises.hook: Must every umbrella belong to a full group?
premises.visible_action: Seventeen identical rods enter four-slot racks; one slides into a clearly marked remainder tray.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Division can produce complete groups and a remainder.
premises.gate: State whole-object grouping; do not imply fractional division is impossible.

premises.title: The Shadow That Outgrew Its Owner
premises.premise: A puppeteer needs a small shadow to fit a screen, but moving the puppet toward the lamp makes the silhouette larger. Comparing fixed lamp-screen geometry reveals which adjustment restores the intended size.
premises.hook: Why did my tiny puppet become a giant?
premises.visible_action: A point lamp stays fixed as a stick puppet slides between lamp and screen; boundary rays trace its shadow.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Shadow size depends on the relative positions of source, object, and screen.
premises.gate: Review geometrical-optics assumptions; use an idealized point source and safe animated lighting.

premises.title: The Boat Made of a Sinking Block
premises.premise: A model builder wants a clay cargo carrier to float, but a compact lump sinks in the simulation. Reshaping the same material into a hollow hull changes displaced water, allowing a reviewed buoyancy explanation.
premises.hook: Same clay, different shape: will it still sink?
premises.visible_action: A clay block morphs into a hollow boat; a transparent waterline and displaced-volume overlay update together.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Floating depends on weight and buoyant force, not material name alone.
premises.gate: Validate buoyancy and hull assumptions; avoid unsupervised water-play instructions.

premises.title: The Traveling Pulse
premises.premise: A messenger wants to send a signal along a row of spring-linked blocks, but assumes a marked block must travel to the receiver. The pulse arrives while the marked block oscillates near its starting position.
premises.hook: Does the messenger move, or does the message?
premises.visible_action: A colored block rocks locally as a compression pulse travels through a spring-linked row.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A wave can transfer a disturbance while local material moves differently.
premises.gate: Specify a longitudinal mechanical-wave model; do not generalize it to all waves.

premises.title: The Vanishing Puddle Ledger
premises.premise: A sidewalk custodian wants to account for a shrinking puddle, but a floor-level camera makes the water seem destroyed. A cutaway follows water into surrounding air and closes the illustrated matter ledger.
premises.hook: Where did the puddle go when nobody wiped it up?
premises.visible_action: A puddle outline contracts while a symbolic water counter moves from surface to air, preserving the displayed total.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Evaporation changes where water is and its phase; it does not erase it.
premises.gate: Review evaporation depiction; label particle icons symbolic and avoid promising a drying time.

premises.title: The Glass With an Outside Leak
premises.premise: A diner wants to identify water appearing outside a cold glass, but blames a nonexistent crack. A split view traces moisture from nearby air onto the cooled outer surface.
premises.hook: How can a sealed glass leak on the outside?
premises.visible_action: A magnified outer glass surface gains droplets while a colored inside-liquid marker remains inside the vessel.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Condensation can form from moisture in air on a sufficiently cool surface.
premises.gate: Review dew-point conditions and distinguish condensation from spills or real leaks.

premises.title: The Compass Delivery Route
premises.premise: A courier needs to orient a compass beside a magnet, but expects its needle to point directly at the nearest end from every position. Moving the compass around a reviewed field diagram reveals the changing direction.
premises.hook: Will the needle point the same way over here?
premises.visible_action: A compass follows a circular track around a bar magnet; its needle rotates and leaves directional stamps.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Magnetic-field direction varies with position around a magnet.
premises.gate: Review field geometry; use animation only and avoid small-magnet handling instructions.

premises.title: The Air That Pushes Back
premises.premise: A mechanic wants to compress a sealed pocket of air, but treats the empty-looking cylinder as empty. A piston-and-particle cutaway shows the resistance increase as the available volume decreases under stated conditions.
premises.hook: If this chamber is empty, what is pushing back?
premises.visible_action: A piston shortens a sealed chamber; symbolic particles rebound and a qualitative pressure indicator rises.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Air occupies space and can exert pressure.
premises.gate: Review pressure-temperature assumptions; do not provide pressurized-device construction steps.

premises.title: The Bent Straw Detective
premises.premise: An illustrator wants to draw a straw crossing a water surface, but a straight copied line misses its apparent bend. A ray overlay distinguishes the physical straw from the changing path of light.
premises.hook: Did the straw bend, or did the light change direction?
premises.visible_action: A rigid straw stays still while selected light rays bend at the water boundary and an apparent image shifts.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Refraction can change the apparent position of a submerged object.
premises.gate: Review refractive geometry and observer position; mark apparent and physical locations separately.

premises.title: The Missing Return Path
premises.premise: A lamp designer wants a toy circuit symbol to light, but draws only a wire from the source to the bulb. Completing the return path in the simulation closes the circuit and lights the indicator.
premises.hook: One wire reaches the lamp. What is still missing?
premises.visible_action: A schematic wire grows toward a source terminal; the lamp icon changes only when the loop is closed.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A simple closed circuit includes a complete conducting path.
premises.gate: Use a symbolic low-voltage simulation; no mains wiring, exposed-battery, or short-circuit instructions.

premises.title: The Marble That Cannot Climb Home
premises.premise: A marble needs to reach its starting height after rolling through a rough valley, but slows before the far summit. An energy-accounting overlay includes frictional transfer instead of inventing missing energy.
premises.hook: Why does the second hill keep winning?
premises.visible_action: A marble rolls down and up a track; motion and height indicators change while a thermal-transfer ledger grows.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Friction changes how energy is distributed and limits mechanical motion.
premises.gate: Review energy accounting; avoid depicting energy as destroyed or heat as a material fluid.

premises.title: The Maze With a Waiting Line
premises.premise: A search robot wants the shortest route through an unweighted tile maze, but repeatedly chases the most tempting corridor. Expanding a first-in-first-out frontier one layer at a time finds a shortest route.
premises.hook: Which square should the robot visit next?
premises.visible_action: Tile coordinates enter and leave a visible queue; distance rings spread outward before the final path lights.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Breadth-first search explores unweighted routes in increasing edge count.
premises.gate: Keep every edge equal in cost and distinguish exploration from the final route.

premises.title: The Four-Bit Lantern
premises.premise: A technician must display thirteen using four binary lamps, but initially reads 1101 as ordinary decimal digits. Labeling lamp weights eight, four, two, and one makes the lit total clear.
premises.hook: Four lamps, thirteen signals: how?
premises.visible_action: Four weighted lamp blocks toggle; illuminated weights fall into an addition tray showing thirteen.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Binary place value uses powers of two.
premises.gate: Use unsigned four-bit integers and avoid implying this explains all computer number formats.

premises.title: The Parcel Queue Remembers
premises.premise: A dispatcher must sort parcels by destination while preserving arrival order within each destination, but an unstable reshuffle swaps two customers. Numbered tags make the mistake visible and a stable sort preserves both requirements.
premises.hook: These parcels match. Which one should leave first?
premises.visible_action: Colored parcels sort into destination lanes while tiny arrival-number badges remain attached and comparable.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Stable sorting preserves the prior order of equal-key items.
premises.gate: State the sort key and tie-order requirement; do not claim stability is always necessary.

premises.title: The Crowded Hash Locker
premises.premise: A librarian wants fast storage lookup, but two book keys map to the same locker. A visible collision list retains both books and a full-key check retrieves the requested one.
premises.hook: Two keys, one locker: did a book disappear?
premises.visible_action: Key cards pass through a toy modulo machine; colliding cards stack in one bucket and are compared individually.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Hash collisions require an explicit resolution and key-checking strategy.
premises.gate: Use a toy hash table; do not conflate indexing hashes with cryptographic security.

premises.title: The Double-Counted Visitor
premises.premise: A curator wants a visitor total from two entrance logs, but counts a returning badge twice. Matching a defined visit identifier and showing the excluded duplicate produces a transparent total.
premises.hook: Is this a new visitor, or the same badge again?
premises.visible_action: Two record streams merge; matching visit-ID cards align, and duplicate records move into an audit tray.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Deduplication depends on a clearly defined identity and counting rule.
premises.gate: Use invented records; explain that people, visits, and devices are different counting units.

premises.title: The Two Endings Merge
premises.premise: Two animators must combine edits to one story, but both changed the same final line. A branch diagram preserves their versions and highlights the conflict so they can choose a deliberate combined ending.
premises.hook: Which ending did we actually agree to keep?
premises.visible_action: A timeline forks into two colored branches; conflicting text blocks meet at a highlighted merge checkpoint.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Version control preserves change history; conflicting intent still needs a decision.
premises.gate: Use invented text and a generic workflow; exact platform commands require separate review.

premises.title: The Stripe Compressor Meets Confetti
premises.premise: A messenger wants to shrink an image description, but a repeated-run code that helps stripes grows bulky on alternating pixels. Comparing encoded lengths reveals when this particular compression scheme helps.
premises.hook: Can the same shortcut make one picture bigger?
premises.visible_action: Long same-color strips become count-color tokens; alternating pixels produce many small tokens and a longer ruler.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Compression effectiveness depends on both the data and the encoding overhead.
premises.gate: Specify token costs and a reversible toy encoding; avoid claims about all compression.

premises.title: The Disappearing Checkerboard
premises.premise: A camera robot wants to capture fine stripes, but its sparse sample points miss alternating details. Sliding the sampling grid changes the recorded pattern and exposes the ambiguity.
premises.hook: Why do the stripes vanish when the camera steps back?
premises.visible_action: A sampling lattice moves over a striped panel; selected points build a coarse image beside the original.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Sampling can lose detail or create misleading patterns when resolution is insufficient.
premises.gate: Define the synthetic pattern and sampler; real-camera optics need additional source review.

premises.title: The Last Search Arrives First
premises.premise: A search box must show results for the newest query, but a slower old request arrives after a newer one and overwrites it. Request identifiers let the display ignore stale responses.
premises.hook: Why did the old answer replace the new one?
premises.visible_action: Two query envelopes race along unequal tracks; a current-request gate rejects the late obsolete envelope.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Asynchronous completion order may differ from request order.
premises.gate: Use a toy interface; actual cancellation, errors, and server behavior vary.

premises.title: The Recommendation Echo Room
premises.premise: A curator wants a varied animation playlist, but a toy recommender only learns from the clips it already chose to show. An exploration lane exposes unseen options and reveals the feedback loop.
premises.hook: What can this system learn from a choice it never offered?
premises.visible_action: A recommendation carousel feeds clicks back into itself until an exploratory card enters from a separate lane.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Observed preferences can reflect what a system chose to expose.
premises.gate: Label the algorithm invented; do not imply all recommendation systems behave identically.

premises.title: The Closed-Notebook Bridge
premises.premise: A learner wants to know whether a diagram is understood, but recognizes every label only while the page is open. Rebuilding it from blank blocks reveals gaps that can be checked against the source.
premises.hook: Can you rebuild it after the page disappears?
premises.visible_action: A labeled diagram folds away; blank blocks are assembled from memory and mismatches glow during comparison.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A retrieval attempt can reveal gaps that looking at the answer hides.
premises.gate: Review learning-science claims; make no guaranteed retention or grade promises.

premises.title: The Review Calendar Has Gaps
premises.premise: A student needs several chances to revisit a vocabulary set, but piles every review into one afternoon. A calendar animation redistributes the same planned sessions and records what needs another look.
premises.hook: What if the next review happened on another day?
premises.visible_action: Equal-duration review blocks move from a crowded day into separated calendar slots; recall checks leave small flags.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A study plan can schedule repeated reviews across time and adjust from recall.
premises.gate: Review spacing evidence; no universally optimal interval or fixed learning outcome is claimed.

premises.title: The Example Loses Its Training Wheels
premises.premise: A learner wants to solve a new worked problem, but copying every displayed step hides which choices are understood. Successively removing selected steps invites the learner to supply and check them.
premises.hook: This time, one step is missing. What belongs here?
premises.visible_action: A completed solution scroll replaces first one, then several blocks with empty sockets that accept learner choices.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Worked examples can become practice when support is deliberately reduced.
premises.gate: Review scaffolding claims; keep example difficulty and prerequisite knowledge explicit.

premises.title: The Mixed-Tool Workshop
premises.premise: An apprentice wants to choose the right method for each puzzle, but grouped practice lets the shelf label make every choice. Mixed puzzle cards remove that cue and require a reason before selecting a tool.
premises.hook: Which tool fits when the shelf stops telling you?
premises.visible_action: Three symbolic tools face shuffled shape puzzles; a reason card must snap in before a tool can move.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Choosing a method is a separate skill from carrying out a known method.
premises.gate: Present a limited study illustration; benefits of mixed practice depend on the material.

premises.title: The Confidence Stamp Audit
premises.premise: A quiz maker wants to judge readiness, but stamps every familiar-looking answer as certain. Comparing confidence stamps with checked answers reveals which judgments need recalibration.
premises.hook: How sure are you before the answer flips over?
premises.visible_action: Answer cards receive small confidence meters; cards flip and sort into confidence-versus-correctness bins.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Compare confidence with checked performance instead of relying on familiarity alone.
premises.gate: Use invented quiz scores and avoid labeling a learner or inferring clinical traits.

premises.title: The Museum of Useful Mistakes
premises.premise: A learner wants to stop repeating one algebra slip, but an answer-only notebook hides where it begins. An error exhibit pairs the mistaken step, its cause, and a corrected counterexample.
premises.hook: Which tiny step broke the whole solution?
premises.visible_action: A solution strip pauses at one sign change; a magnifier extracts it into a three-panel error card.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Recording the specific error can make the next check more targeted.
premises.gate: Check all mathematics; frame mistakes as information rather than personal failure.

premises.title: The Assignment With No First Door
premises.premise: A student wants to start a large project, but a single giant task block has no obvious entry point. Breaking out a concrete first action opens a path to the remaining steps.
premises.hook: What can you do before you can do the whole thing?
premises.visible_action: A towering assignment block unfolds into small action tiles, beginning with opening the brief and extracting one requirement.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A large goal becomes easier to initiate when its next action is explicit.
premises.gate: Offer an organizational example, not mental-health treatment or a promise against procrastination.

premises.title: The Explain-It Puppet
premises.premise: A learner wants to teach a process to a puppet, but a confident explanation skips the step that connects input to output. The puppet asks what changes next, exposing the gap for source checking.
premises.hook: What happens between those two boxes?
premises.visible_action: A puppet follows a block diagram until a missing connector stops it; the learner adds a verified transition.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Explaining a sequence can expose missing links in understanding.
premises.gate: Do not invent the missing explanation; any factual lesson needs its own source check.

premises.title: The Note With a Broken Tether
premises.premise: A researcher wants to reuse a striking claim, but its note has lost the original source and surrounding context. Reattaching a citation card and checking the passage distinguishes support from speculation.
premises.hook: Where did this sentence come from?
premises.visible_action: A claim block dangles from a severed line; source, date, and context cards reconnect before it enters an outline.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Useful research notes preserve a path back to supporting evidence.
premises.gate: Use invented sources or verified public ones; a citation alone does not establish truth.

premises.title: The Practice Session Has a Finish Line
premises.premise: A learner wants a manageable practice session, but an undefined goal keeps expanding whenever another exercise appears. Choosing a small task, a checking step, and a stopping point produces a reviewable session.
premises.hook: How will you know this practice session is done?
premises.visible_action: An endless conveyor gains a gate after a selected set of exercises; a final check card unlocks the exit.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Define both the task and what completion looks like before expanding a session.
premises.gate: Do not prescribe universal attention spans or imply one routine suits everyone.

premises.title: The Pronoun With Two Owners
premises.premise: A courier must deliver a note saying Alex told Sam that their bag was missing, but cannot tell whose bag it means. Replacing the ambiguous pronoun with the intended name unlocks the correct route.
premises.hook: Whose bag is actually missing?
premises.visible_action: Two stick figures tug on one pronoun bubble until a named label connects it to a single bag.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: An explicit noun can resolve ambiguity when a pronoun has multiple possible referents.
premises.gate: Use invented people and preserve intentional ambiguity when it serves the author.

premises.title: The Listener Sends a Mirror
premises.premise: A builder wants to carry out a request, but assumes that make it lighter means use a paler color. Paraphrasing the intended change reveals that the requester meant reduce weight before any work begins.
premises.hook: Lighter in color, or lighter to carry?
premises.visible_action: One word forks into a paint swatch and a weighing scale; a confirming reply locks the chosen branch.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Checking meaning can prevent action on an ambiguous request.
premises.gate: Do not imply confirmation is required for every ordinary low-risk phrase.

premises.title: The Comma Changes the Guest List
premises.premise: An event host wants to label snacks for guests, but an unpunctuated line combines categories in two possible ways. Brackets and punctuation make the intended grouping visible before the labels print.
premises.hook: How many groups did this sentence invite?
premises.visible_action: A sentence splits into movable phrase blocks; alternative brackets form different groupings and matching guest icons.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Punctuation and sentence structure help readers identify intended grouping.
premises.gate: Check the chosen sentence for genuine alternative readings rather than a contrived grammar rule.

premises.title: The Same Request Wears Two Coats
premises.premise: A teammate needs the same missing file from a close colleague and an unfamiliar organizer, but copies a context-heavy shorthand message to both. Adding necessary context adapts the second request without changing its purpose.
premises.hook: What does this reader already know?
premises.visible_action: A compact request bubble gains file name, deadline context, and greeting blocks as its audience marker changes.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Adapt context and tone to the reader while preserving the underlying request.
premises.gate: Avoid treating one cultural register as universally correct or inventing the sender’s feelings.

premises.title: The Idiom Meets a Literal Painter
premises.premise: A translator wants to convey that a task is easy, but a literal painting of an idiom produces an irrelevant object. A meaning card bridges to plain language and, only after review, an appropriate target-language expression.
premises.hook: Should we translate the picture or the meaning?
premises.visible_action: An idiom bubble becomes a literal sketch, then passes through a meaning gate before a new expression appears.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: An idiom’s intended meaning may not survive word-for-word translation.
premises.gate: Have a fluent reviewer verify any actual language pair and regional usage.

premises.title: The Directions Need a Landmark
premises.premise: A visitor wants to find a room, but left-right instructions change meaning when the starting orientation changes. A fixed landmark and a simple route sketch give the visitor a stable reference.
premises.hook: Left from whose point of view?
premises.visible_action: A rotating stick figure follows conflicting arrows until a fixed entrance icon anchors the map.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Directions become clearer when the starting point and frame of reference are explicit.
premises.gate: Use a fictional indoor route; do not present it as accessible or emergency navigation advice.

premises.title: The Interrupted Thought Queue
premises.premise: A meeting group wants every proposal considered, but overlapping speech bubbles bury a quiet unfinished idea. A visible speaking queue and a shared written option let the group return to each contribution.
premises.hook: Whose idea fell between the speech bubbles?
premises.visible_action: Speech bubbles collide, then settle into a queue; a text card joins through a parallel written lane.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A communication process can create more than one way to contribute.
premises.gate: Do not equate silence with lack of ideas or prescribe one speaking style for everyone.

premises.title: The Icon That Meant Two Things
premises.premise: A designer wants a button understood without explanation, but two viewers read the same star as favorite and rating. Pairing it with a clear label and checking the intended action resolves the prototype confusion.
premises.hook: Will this star save it, or score it?
premises.visible_action: One star button forks into two predicted outcomes; a text label snaps beneath the selected action.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: An icon’s meaning may need context, labeling, and user checking.
premises.gate: Do not claim symbols are universally intuitive; real-interface accessibility needs review.

premises.title: The Feedback Arrow Finds a Target
premises.premise: An editor wants a scene improved, but the note make it better gives the animator no usable target. Pointing to a specific confusing moment and explaining its effect creates an actionable revision request.
premises.hook: Which moment needs to change?
premises.visible_action: A vague cloud shrinks into an arrow on one frame, followed by observation and desired-effect cards.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Useful feedback identifies the location, observed problem, and intended result.
premises.gate: Keep observations separate from personal judgments; do not invent consensus about quality.

premises.title: The Summary Drops Its Anchor
premises.premise: A reporter wants to shorten a discussion, but cuts away the condition that made a proposal acceptable. A comparison restores the condition and labels remaining disagreement instead of inventing a unanimous decision.
premises.hook: What disappeared when the meeting became one sentence?
premises.visible_action: A long transcript folds into summary cards; a dangling condition tag signals a lost qualification.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A concise summary should preserve material conditions, uncertainty, and disagreement.
premises.gate: Use an invented meeting; do not attribute decisions or approval to real people.

premises.title: The Handoff With No Handle
premises.premise: A team must pass a finished asset to the next person, but the package contains a file with no version, owner, or next step. A handoff card supplies those details and lets work continue.
premises.hook: The file arrived. What should happen to it now?
premises.visible_action: A parcel stalls between desks until version, owner, and next-action tags click onto its handle.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A handoff needs enough context for the receiver to take the next action.
premises.gate: Use invented project details and avoid implying tags replace actual access checks.

premises.title: The Narrowest Gate
premises.premise: A production line needs more finished frames, but extra workers feed a review gate that can process only one frame at a time. Measuring the queue reveals the constraint and shifting effort there improves the toy flow.
premises.hook: Why is working faster making this pile bigger?
premises.visible_action: Wide upstream conveyors dump frames before a narrow gate; counters track arrivals, departures, and queue length.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Improving a non-constraining step may only increase waiting work.
premises.gate: State the simulated arrival and service rates; real organizational bottlenecks require observation.

premises.title: The Checklist Remembers the Quiet Step
premises.premise: A recurring export must include subtitles, but the dramatic animation work distracts the operator from the final accessibility check. A short checklist puts the overlooked step at the point of export.
premises.hook: Which small step disappears when the big work feels done?
premises.visible_action: An export lever pauses beside three checkboxes; the subtitle preview opens before the lever completes its path.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A checklist can make a repeatable, easily forgotten step visible at the right moment.
premises.gate: Keep the checklist specific; checking a box alone does not verify subtitle quality.

premises.title: The Task That Waited on Tomorrow
premises.premise: A team wants to finish a demo Friday, but schedules the sound mix before the narration is approved. A dependency graph makes the impossible order visible and moves approval ahead of the mix.
premises.hook: Can this step start before its input exists?
premises.visible_action: Task cards connect by arrows; a downstream card hits a locked gate until its predecessor turns ready.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Dependencies constrain which work can start and when.
premises.gate: Dates and durations are invented; do not imply a dependency chart predicts all delays.

premises.title: The Five Almost-Finished Posters
premises.premise: A designer wants five completed posters, but keeps switching whenever a new idea appears. A visible limit on active drafts lets one poster cross the finish line before another enters.
premises.hook: Why are five busy canvases producing zero finished posters?
premises.visible_action: Five half-painted boards compete for one brush; an active-work gate admits only the chosen small set.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Limiting simultaneous work can make completion and blocked items easier to see.
premises.gate: No universal productivity gain or ideal work-in-progress limit is asserted.

premises.title: The Reversible Door
premises.premise: A product team wants to test two layouts, but treats a replaceable mockup as if it were a permanent public launch. Marking reversibility and consequence lets them try the mockup while reserving review for the lasting decision.
premises.hook: Which door lets us walk back out?
premises.visible_action: Two doors display undo paths; a sandbox preview loops back while a public-release door requires a review key.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Decision process should reflect consequences, reversibility, and actual authority.
premises.gate: Reversibility never substitutes for required permission, privacy, or safety review.

premises.title: The Request That Grew Extra Wheels
premises.premise: An animator wants to deliver a short loop, but each casual suggestion silently adds another scene. A visible scope card separates the agreed deliverable from optional additions and prompts a real tradeoff.
premises.hook: When did a loop become a whole episode?
premises.visible_action: A small project cart accumulates unapproved wheels and trailers; optional cards detach into a separate review queue.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Changing scope should trigger an explicit choice about priorities, time, and approval.
premises.gate: Do not assign commitments or reject stakeholder requests on anyone’s behalf.

premises.title: The Assumption Under the Floor
premises.premise: A planner wants to compare two production routes, but one estimate silently assumes existing voice recordings. Pulling up the floorboard reveals the assumption and recalculating both routes makes the comparison usable.
premises.hook: What is this estimate standing on?
premises.visible_action: Two timelines rest on foundation blocks; removing a missing-recording assumption lengthens only the affected path.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: An estimate is easier to evaluate when its key assumptions are visible.
premises.gate: Use invented times and costs; avoid presenting the toy forecast as a real quote.

premises.title: The Definition-of-Done Turnstile
premises.premise: A team wants to close a task, but one person means rendered while another means reviewed and delivered. A shared set of observable completion checks aligns the label before the task exits.
premises.hook: Done in whose sense of the word?
premises.visible_action: A completed frame approaches a turnstile with render, review, and delivery slots; only verified tokens open it.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Define completion in observable terms before relying on a status label.
premises.gate: Use task-appropriate criteria; do not imply all projects need the same approval chain.

premises.title: The Retrospective Rewinds One Frame
premises.premise: A team wants a recurring failure to stop, but a retrospective jumps from the outcome straight to blame. Rewinding a concrete timeline exposes a missing check and yields one testable process adjustment.
premises.hook: What happened just before the mistake became expensive?
premises.visible_action: A timeline rewinds to a missing checkpoint; an alternate run adds the checkpoint and displays a measurable result.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Review a sequence of events and test a specific change instead of guessing motives.
premises.gate: Avoid identifying real individuals or claiming one process change guarantees prevention.

premises.title: The Cupboard Behind the Cupboard
premises.premise: A cook wants to find a frequently used lid, but deep stacks hide it behind rarely used pieces. A cutaway separates visible access space from hidden storage and gives the lid a reachable, labeled slot.
premises.hook: How many things must move before this lid can leave?
premises.visible_action: A cupboard becomes transparent; ghost paths count obstacles before a vertical divider gives each lid a direct exit.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Storage usefulness depends on retrieval effort as well as total capacity.
premises.gate: Use a toy cupboard; do not prescribe load limits or physical accessibility from the animation.

premises.title: The Keys Arrive Before the Search
premises.premise: A housemate wants to leave on time, but keys land in a different place after every arrival. A small landing tray at the actual entry route creates a repeatable return path and ends the fictional search loop.
premises.hook: Where did the keys go before you needed them?
premises.visible_action: A stick figure enters along three past routes; dotted key trails converge on a tray placed beside the used entrance.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Put an item’s return point where the relevant routine actually happens.
premises.gate: Present one household experiment, not a universal habit or attention intervention.

premises.title: The Drawer That Counts Footprints
premises.premise: A dresser wants six folded shirts to fit without hiding the bottom ones, but each fold uses a different footprint. A measured toy folding template makes the available drawer layout visible before packing.
premises.hook: Are these shirts too many, or just packed differently?
premises.visible_action: Flat cloth rectangles fold along guides into equal footprints, then stand in a grid inside a transparent drawer.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Consistent dimensions can make storage capacity and visibility easier to reason about.
premises.gate: Use idealized cloth dimensions; real fabrics, drawer clearance, and preferences vary.

premises.title: The Cable Name Travels to Both Ends
premises.premise: A desk owner wants to identify a device cable, but a tangled bundle hides its destination. In a de-energized diagram, matching labels at both ends reveal the connection without guesswork.
premises.hook: Which of these ends belongs to that screen?
premises.visible_action: Colored label pairs attach to a symbolic cable network; selecting one end highlights the complete path and matching end.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A useful connection label can be read at the point where identification is needed.
premises.gate: Animation is an identification diagram only; no live-electrical handling or disconnection instructions.

premises.title: The Maybe Box Has a Date
premises.premise: A household wants to decide whether a few rarely used objects still belong in its storage, but repeated indecision keeps returning them to the main shelf. A dated review box records the question for a later deliberate decision.
premises.hook: Can this decision wait somewhere that is not the whole shelf?
premises.visible_action: Three uncertain objects enter a transparent box with a review date; the shelf clears while a calendar marker remains.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A deferred decision benefits from a bounded place and an explicit review point.
premises.gate: Do not imply permission to discard, donate, or sell items; ownership and sentiment remain with the user.

premises.title: The Borrowed Stapler Leaves a Shadow
premises.premise: A shared household wants to know where a stapler went, but an empty drawer contains no clue. A simple borrowed-item card identifies the current holder and expected return without needing a search through rooms.
premises.hook: The stapler is gone. What could stay behind?
premises.visible_action: A stapler leaves its outlined drawer slot; a borrower card slides into the outline and later returns with the object.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Shared storage can track temporary exceptions without pretending the item is lost.
premises.gate: Use fictional housemates and avoid tracking people or collecting unnecessary personal information.

premises.title: The Pantry Echo Purchase
premises.premise: A shopper wants to buy only the missing supplies, but a hidden extra packet causes another duplicate purchase. A front-facing count card and a quick stock check align the list with what is already present.
premises.hook: Is the cupboard empty, or is the last packet hiding?
premises.visible_action: Duplicate packets emerge from behind boxes; inventory counters feed a shopping list that updates before the cart moves.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A purchase list is more useful when it reflects visible, current stock.
premises.gate: This is quantity organization only; do not infer food safety, freshness, or dietary suitability.

premises.title: The Floor Cleaned Too Soon
premises.premise: A tidier wants a small room reset, but clears the floor before emptying a tabletop and immediately covers it again. Sequencing the fictional tasks by where displaced objects go prevents the repeated pass.
premises.hook: Which task makes work for the task you just finished?
premises.visible_action: Table objects fall into a floor work zone; a dependency arrow rearranges two task cards and removes a repeated sweep.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Sequence tasks with attention to what each step changes for the next one.
premises.gate: Show generic dry tidying only; no chemical mixing, sanitation, or hazardous cleanup guidance.

premises.title: The Paper Lands in One Inbox
premises.premise: A resident wants to find a recent event flyer, but loose papers arrive on every surface. One incoming-paper tray separates unprocessed items from a small set of named destinations and makes the flyer findable.
premises.hook: Is this paper waiting for a decision, or already filed?
premises.visible_action: Paper glides from door and bag into one tray, then routes to action, reference, or personally reviewed discard slots.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Separate incoming material from material that already has a decided place.
premises.gate: Use harmless invented papers; legal, financial, and identity-record retention requires separate guidance.

premises.title: The Cabinet Door Needs Its Own Space
premises.premise: A room planner wants a new storage unit to fit, but checks only the closed footprint and blocks its opening door. A swept-area overlay reveals the collision and a revised toy layout restores usable clearance.
premises.hook: It fits when shut. Can it open?
premises.visible_action: A cabinet door rotates through a translucent arc that collides with a desk; the desk slides outside the arc.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A layout must account for movement and use, not just closed-object footprints.
premises.gate: Use a fictional dimensioned room; actual accessibility and installation requirements need review.

premises.title: The Raindrop Has a Downhill Address
premises.premise: A raindrop wants to reach the river in a miniature landscape, but a flat map hides the ridges separating drainage routes. Raising the relief model shows its downhill path and the boundary of its watershed.
premises.hook: Which river gets this drop?
premises.visible_action: A flat map lifts into terrain blocks; blue tracer drops follow slopes on opposite sides of a ridge.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Watershed boundaries follow terrain that directs surface runoff toward different outlets.
premises.gate: Review hydrology; label simplified terrain and omit flood predictions or contaminated-water handling.

premises.title: The Pollinator Has More Than One Stop
premises.premise: A gardener wants to understand why one flowering plant gets visits, but watches only that plant and misses the network around it. Following a reviewed example pollinator between flowers reveals interacting needs and timing.
premises.hook: Where did this visitor come from before reaching your flower?
premises.visible_action: A small insect icon follows timed flower-to-flower paths while a calendar band exposes periods with few open blooms.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Pollination can be understood as interactions among organisms over space and time.
premises.gate: Select a real reviewed plant-pollinator example; do not assume all insects or flowers play identical roles.

premises.title: The Habitat Islands Need a Crossing
premises.premise: An animal icon wants to reach another suitable habitat patch, but development separates the patches in a toy landscape. Comparing possible connections shows why the value of a corridor depends on the species and surrounding conditions.
premises.hook: A green line joins the patches. Can this animal use it?
premises.visible_action: Habitat blocks separate; candidate corridors appear with different width and cover markers, and a species card filters them.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Connectivity depends on the needs of the organism and the quality of the route.
premises.gate: Review a specific ecological context; do not promise a generic corridor restores biodiversity.

premises.title: The Fallen Leaf Changes Teams
premises.premise: A park keeper wants to trace a leaf after it falls, but stops the story when it becomes unrecognizable. A reviewed decomposer sequence follows matter through smaller pieces and biological processes without calling it disappearance.
premises.hook: When a leaf stops looking like a leaf, is its story over?
premises.visible_action: A leaf breaks into labeled stages; matter-counter symbols move through a simplified decomposer network and surrounding environment.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Decomposition transforms and redistributes organic matter through ecological processes.
premises.gate: Review matter pathways and timescales; avoid implying every leaf follows one identical route.

premises.title: The Food Web Loses One Knot
premises.premise: A museum guide wants to explain a predator’s role, but a single straight food chain hides alternative connections. Removing one node from a reviewed web highlights possible indirect effects and the limits of a simple prediction.
premises.hook: Which other lines move when this knot disappears?
premises.visible_action: A network of organism nodes stretches as one node fades; direct links highlight before uncertain downstream paths appear dashed.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Food webs include indirect relationships that make ecological effects context-dependent.
premises.gate: Use a sourced ecosystem; distinguish documented effects from hypothetical outcomes.

premises.title: The Two Seasonal Clocks
premises.premise: A migrating visitor wants to arrive when a food resource is available, but two seasonal timing bands shift differently in the model. Aligning the bands reveals a possible mismatch without claiming it happens for every species.
premises.hook: What if dinner’s clock moves faster than the guest’s?
premises.visible_action: Two calendar wheels rotate at different offsets; overlapping resource and arrival windows shrink or widen.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Interacting species can depend on overlapping seasonal events.
premises.gate: Choose a primary-sourced example; climate and biological responses vary by species and place.

premises.title: The Shade Moves Across the Square
premises.premise: A planner wants to compare two public-square designs, but judges tree shade from one static noon image. A time sweep shows where shadows travel and what the simplified model leaves unmeasured.
premises.hook: Does this bench stay shaded after the camera stops?
premises.visible_action: A sun indicator crosses an arc while tree and structure shadows sweep over a tiled square and a marked bench.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Shade is spatial and time-dependent; one snapshot cannot describe a whole day.
premises.gate: Review solar geometry and any heat claims; make no health or local comfort guarantees.

premises.title: The Hitchhiking Seed Trail
premises.premise: A habitat educator wants to explain how an introduced plant might reach a new site, but a map showing only established patches misses transport links. A reviewed fictionalized pathway highlights prevention questions without teaching removal or dispersal.
premises.hook: How did the next patch begin so far away?
premises.visible_action: Seed symbols follow dashed routes on equipment and transport icons; arrival points connect to a source-verification card.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Species movement can involve human transport pathways as well as nearby spread.
premises.gate: Use region-specific official guidance; avoid identification, eradication, handling, or deliberate release instructions.

premises.title: The Shopping Bag’s Hidden Timeline
premises.premise: A shopper wants to compare two bags, but the picture at checkout hides production, repeated use, and disposal. A boundary slider exposes which lifecycle stages are included before any environmental comparison is made.
premises.hook: Which parts of this bag’s life did the comparison leave out?
premises.visible_action: Two bags unfold into timelines; a movable analysis window includes or excludes production, use cycles, and end-of-life stages.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Environmental comparisons depend on boundaries, assumptions, use, and local end-of-life conditions.
premises.gate: Use reviewed lifecycle sources before quantitative or purchase claims; do not declare a universal winner.

premises.title: The Night Map Gains a Dimmer
premises.premise: A town wants useful nighttime lighting, but a plan treating every lit area alike hides where light travels beyond its intended target. Comparing shielded and unshielded symbolic beams frames a reviewed discussion of tradeoffs.
premises.hook: Where does the light go after it misses the path?
premises.visible_action: Lamp cones sweep across a path, windows, and habitat icons; beam boundaries and timing settings change in parallel panels.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Lighting design can consider direction, timing, purpose, and effects beyond the intended area.
premises.gate: Review ecology and local lighting requirements; make no public-safety or health claims without evidence.

premises.title: The Caption That Lost the Speaker
premises.premise: A viewer wants to follow a scene without its audio, but the caption shows words with no indication of which offscreen figure spoke. Reviewed speaker identification and meaningful sound labels restore the missing context.
premises.hook: Who said that when neither mouth was on screen?
premises.visible_action: Two offscreen speech paths feed a caption strip; speaker labels attach and a relevant door-sound cue appears.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Captions may need speaker and meaningful sound information as well as spoken words.
premises.gate: Review caption standards and actual audio; do not claim compliance from one example.

premises.title: The Chart Cannot Spend Color Twice
premises.premise: A reader wants to identify the two lines in a chart, but color is the only distinction. Adding direct labels and different stroke patterns makes the intended comparison available through more than one visual cue.
premises.hook: If these colors look the same, what else tells them apart?
premises.visible_action: Two colored chart lines shift to equal tones; labels and dash patterns appear while their data remain unchanged.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Do not make color the sole carrier of essential information.
premises.gate: Review applicable accessibility guidance; simulated color changes do not reproduce every person’s vision.

premises.title: The Keyboard Cursor Goes Missing
premises.premise: A keyboard user wants to submit a short form, but invisible focus makes the current control unclear. A visible focus indicator and a reviewed logical order reveal each next target before activation.
premises.hook: Which button would Enter activate right now?
premises.visible_action: A focus ring moves through fields and controls in numbered order; an invisible-focus version runs alongside it.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Keyboard interaction needs a discernible focus position and a usable navigation sequence.
premises.gate: Review real platform behavior and accessibility standards; animation alone is not a keyboard audit.

premises.title: The Motion Dial Keeps the Meaning
premises.premise: A viewer wants the result of an interface action, but a long sweeping animation is uncomfortable or distracting. A reduced-motion version preserves the state change with a quieter transition and equivalent information.
premises.hook: Can this screen explain the change without the swoop?
premises.visible_action: A panel sweep is replaced by an immediate state change and a small status marker in parallel previews.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Motion can be optional while the underlying information and control remain available.
premises.gate: Review reduced-motion guidance; no flashing, simulated symptoms, or claims about all motion sensitivities.

premises.title: The Page Reads in a Different Order
premises.premise: A reader wants a screen-reader-friendly explanation, but visually arranged cards have a confusing underlying sequence. A linear reading trace reveals the mismatch and a revised structure aligns the intended meaning.
premises.hook: What happens when the page is read one item at a time?
premises.visible_action: Numbered content blocks flatten from a grid into a queue; misplaced captions jump beside their associated figures.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Meaningful structure and reading order matter beyond visual placement.
premises.gate: Verify real semantic structure and assistive-technology behavior; this is a conceptual model.

premises.title: The Tiny Button Has Neighbors
premises.premise: A person wants to select one control, but tightly packed small targets make unintended neighbors easy to hit in a toy interface. A revised layout enlarges and separates targets without changing their functions.
premises.hook: Which target did this tap actually hit?
premises.visible_action: A pointer landing area overlaps three small controls; targets expand and spacing opens in the comparison layout.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Interactive target size and spacing affect how forgiving a control layout is.
premises.gate: Review platform-specific guidance; do not invent universal pixel sizes or simulate a disability.

premises.title: The Image Description Has a Job
premises.premise: An author wants to describe a chart image, but a long list of decorative colors omits its relevant finding. Defining the image’s purpose leads to a concise description and an accessible route to the underlying data.
premises.hook: What does the reader need this image to tell them?
premises.visible_action: A decorative-description cloud contracts; chart purpose, finding, and data-access cards connect to the image.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Text alternatives should reflect an image’s purpose in its actual context.
premises.gate: Review the real image and relevant guidance; complex charts may need more than short alternative text.

premises.title: The Timer Erases an Unfinished Form
premises.premise: A user wants to finish a form at their own pace, but an unexpected timeout clears entered information. A reviewed design exposes timing, offers appropriate continuation, and preserves progress where permitted.
premises.hook: Why did the form disappear before the answer was ready?
premises.visible_action: A hidden timer becomes visible; warning and continuation states appear, and entered blocks remain in a protected draft lane.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Time limits should be considered explicitly in accessible interaction design.
premises.gate: Review timing exceptions, privacy, and security constraints; no blanket requirement to retain sensitive entries.

premises.title: The Route Has More Than One Sense
premises.premise: A museum wants visitors to find a gallery, but directions rely only on a spoken announcement. A co-designed prototype pairs clear text, visual landmarks, and other appropriate cues so visitors can choose useful information.
premises.hook: What if the announcement is not available to you?
premises.visible_action: One audio path branches into text signage, a visual map, and a reviewed tactile-cue mockup leading to the same destination.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Important wayfinding information can be offered through complementary modes.
premises.gate: Consult users and qualified access guidance; do not improvise tactile standards or emergency routes.

premises.title: The Instruction Card Opens One Step
premises.premise: A participant wants to assemble a harmless paper model, but a dense paragraph buries the current action among later steps. A plain-language sequence with optional detail exposes one actionable step at a time.
premises.hook: Which action should happen first?
premises.visible_action: A paragraph separates into numbered action cards; an optional-detail tab expands without displacing the current step.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Clear sequencing and optional detail can reduce unnecessary interpretation demands.
premises.gate: Test with intended users; plain language is context-dependent and does not guarantee universal comprehension.

premises.title: The Address Bar Costume Party
premises.premise: A shopper wants to return to a familiar service, but a polished lookalike page imitates its branding. A reviewed example shifts attention from appearance to verifying the destination through an independently known route.
premises.hook: The logo matches. What else needs checking?
premises.visible_action: Two near-identical page mockups slide apart; the destination area enlarges and a known-source route bypasses the suspicious link.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Familiar branding alone does not establish that a page is authentic.
premises.gate: Use reserved example domains only; verify current official guidance and never link to a live deceptive site.

premises.title: The Reused Key Opens Too Many Doors
premises.premise: An account owner wants one compromised fictional account to stay an isolated problem, but a reused password is represented by one key fitting several doors. Distinct symbolic credentials separate the doors in the reviewed security lesson.
premises.hook: Why does one lost key fit every door?
premises.visible_action: A copied key silhouette opens multiple labeled account doors; unique abstract keys replace it without displaying passwords.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Credential reuse can connect the risk across otherwise separate accounts.
premises.gate: Review current official credential guidance; never request, show, store, or transmit real secrets.

premises.title: The Sign-In Prompt Nobody Started
premises.premise: A user wants to respond to a sudden approval prompt, but assumes every notification means an action they initiated. A timeline checks for a matching sign-in and routes the unexplained prompt to official account guidance.
premises.hook: Did you start the sign-in this prompt is asking about?
premises.visible_action: A login event and approval prompt seek a matching timestamp; an unmatched prompt stops before an approval gate.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Unexpected authentication prompts deserve verification rather than automatic approval.
premises.gate: Follow current provider-specific guidance; no codes, recovery credentials, or bypass instructions.

premises.title: The Flashlight Asks for a Guest List
premises.premise: A user wants a simple toy app function, but an unexpected permission request reaches unrelated data. A purpose-to-permission map highlights the mismatch and lets the user review the request before deciding.
premises.hook: Why would this button need those contacts?
premises.visible_action: A flashlight icon connects to a permission panel; unrelated contact-card arrows light up while the stated function remains separate.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Evaluate a permission request against the feature, data involved, and trusted explanation.
premises.gate: Use a fictional app and synthetic data; do not accept permissions or claim any category is always illegitimate.

premises.title: The Price Tag Has a Second Floor
premises.premise: A buyer wants to compare two fictional one-time offers, but one displayed price omits a mandatory fee shown later. Expanding both into itemized totals reveals the actual arithmetic before any purchase choice.
premises.hook: Is the smaller number also the smaller total?
premises.visible_action: Headline prices lift like trapdoors to reveal fee blocks; full totals assemble on equal-width comparison rails.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Compare the complete stated price and commitment, not just the headline number.
premises.gate: Use invented amounts and explicit assumptions; do not infer current laws, taxes, refunds, or subscription terms.

premises.title: The Search Result Wears a Sponsor Badge
premises.premise: A reader wants to understand why a result appears, but treats an advertisement and an unpaid result as identical evidence of quality. Revealing placement labels separates the source of visibility from evaluating the underlying claim.
premises.hook: Did this position come from relevance, payment, or something else?
premises.visible_action: Two result cards gain placement labels; claim evidence is inspected on a separate track from screen position.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Placement and sponsorship are context, not proof that a claim is true or false.
premises.gate: Use generic mockups; verify current labels on any named platform and avoid implying sponsorship means deception.

premises.title: The Photograph Loses Its Calendar
premises.premise: A viewer wants to judge a dramatic claim, but a real-looking image arrives without its original date or context. The story follows source tracing until the image’s earlier setting changes the interpretation.
premises.hook: What if this picture is real but the caption is wrong?
premises.visible_action: A photo card detaches from a dramatic caption; source and date cards reattach as a timeline reveals its earlier context.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Authentic media can still be presented with misleading context.
premises.gate: Use an invented event and owned illustration; do not falsely accuse an actual source or treat metadata alone as proof.

premises.title: The Update Window Arrives by the Wrong Door
premises.premise: A user wants to keep software current, but a web advertisement imitates an update message. The narrative compares its route with the application’s verified update mechanism before any download or installation.
premises.hook: Who opened this update window?
premises.visible_action: A browser ad and a generic application settings panel appear side by side; origin arrows show how each was reached.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Verify the origin and official update route before trusting an update prompt.
premises.gate: Review official vendor guidance; include no executable downloads, live security prompts, or unapproved installation.

premises.title: The Helpful Stranger Wants a Code
premises.premise: An account owner wants to solve an access problem, but an unsolicited helper asks them to read out a sign-in code. A boundary between official recovery and incoming requests stops the disclosure and redirects to a verified support route.
premises.hook: What would this code let the stranger do?
premises.visible_action: A masked code card approaches an outgoing message slot, stops at a verification barrier, and remains concealed.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Treat authentication codes as part of a specific sign-in, not proof for an unsolicited helper.
premises.gate: Verify provider guidance; show no real code and give no impersonation script or account-recovery bypass.

premises.title: The Cloud Mirror Deletes Both Copies
premises.premise: A creator wants a recoverable version of a project, but mistakes a synchronized folder for an independent backup. A toy deletion propagates through the mirror while a separately defined retained version remains available for comparison.
premises.hook: If both copies move together, what happens when one is deleted?
premises.visible_action: Two synchronized folder icons mirror a deletion; a separate version timeline stays visible behind a retention-policy label.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Synchronization and recoverable backup or version retention are different behaviors.
premises.gate: Review the actual service’s recovery and retention behavior; do not delete files or promise recovery.

premises.title: The Exit Plan Meets a Blocked Line
premises.premise: A community center wants a preparedness illustration, but a single unverified arrow crosses a blocked doorway in its fictional floor plan. A qualified review replaces guesswork with an approved, accessible route plan.
premises.hook: Who checked that this arrow leads somewhere usable?
premises.visible_action: A route line stops at a blocked-door icon; the drawing gains a review checkpoint before any revised route is shown.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Preparedness diagrams need verified, locally appropriate routes and accessibility considerations.
premises.gate: Require local fire and accessibility review before publication; teach no improvised evacuation tactics. Do not ask viewers to guess an emergency response or choose an action in a simulated emergency; any response content must come from reviewed official guidance.

premises.title: The Contact Plan Has an Offline Copy
