premises.visible_action: Screens hide panels; blue edge samples pass around; artists move river endpoints; screens lift to reveal a continuous winding shape.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Shared interfaces do not require identical styles.
premises.gate: Use original abstract art; avoid named artist imitation or claims about real collaboration outcomes.

premises.title: The Backpack Swap
premises.premise: Two hikers in a toy landscape cannot reach a lookout because one has a wide pack that catches on narrow arches and the other has a tall pack that hits low beams. They exchange packs at the route junction, each takes the fitting path, and meet at the overlook with the other’s picnic.
premises.hook: We brought the right bags to the wrong paths.
premises.visible_action: Wide pack wedges at an arch; tall pack taps a beam; packs switch; split paths converge at a picnic spot.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Reassigning resources can be better than forcing a fit.
premises.gate: Use toy terrain with no real climbing or packing safety advice.

premises.title: The Audience-Powered Curtain
premises.premise: A puppet crew wants to reveal a show, but the curtain is tied to several short ropes scattered through the seats. Instead of one frantic operator chasing every rope, the crew invites each seated figure to hold a section and raise it together on a visible count.
premises.hook: The show starts when all of us lift.
premises.visible_action: Operator runs between rope ends; ropes droop; seated figures take one each; count cards flip; curtain rises evenly.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Distributing a task can make its timing manageable.
premises.gate: Fictional lightweight puppet curtain; not a real rigging or crowd-participation safety design.

premises.title: The Last Patch of Shade
premises.premise: Three travelers compete to fit beneath one tiny floating shade disc, repeatedly leaving someone exposed in the story’s harsh stylized sun. They stop crowding under it and use three sticks to tilt the disc toward a nearby wall, creating one long stripe of shade where all can rest.
premises.hook: There is enough shade, just in the wrong shape.
premises.visible_action: Disc hovers; figures shuffle; support sticks reposition; disc tilts; a long shadow slides along the ground.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Changing the geometry can change who fits.
premises.gate: Shadow expansion is stylized; validate a physical light model before using this as an optics lesson or heat-safety advice.

premises.title: Across the Breakfast Canyon
premises.premise: A crumb-sized explorer must return a fallen sugar crystal to a bowl, but a cereal bowl’s milk-filled moat blocks the route. The explorer sails in an empty oat shell, steers with a paper splinter, and uses a spoon already spanning the rim as a final ramp.
premises.hook: Breakfast is now a survival-sized map.
premises.visible_action: Oat shell rocks on milk; paper paddle sweeps; a spoon reflects the explorer; sugar crystal rolls gently into the bowl.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A familiar surface can become a new landscape at another scale.
premises.gate: Keep the traveler fantastical; do not encourage placing toys, paper, or unknown objects in food.

premises.title: The Sweater Mountain Rescue
premises.premise: A tiny traveler wants to retrieve a lost flag caught on a sweater, but every knitted loop looks like the same hill. They follow a single contrasting thread through the fabric, reach the flag, and discover the mountain rises only because a sleeping pet is breathing beneath it.
premises.hook: This mountain is breathing.
premises.visible_action: Traveler climbs yarn loops; colored thread snakes between stitches; fabric rises and falls; camera widens to a resting pet-shaped silhouette.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A reliable trail can help in a repeating landscape.
premises.gate: Toy-scale fantasy; no climbing, pet handling, or textile safety instruction.

premises.title: The Printer-Paper Waterfall
premises.premise: A paper-sized messenger must carry a seal across a desk before a harmless sheet dispenser fills it with blank pages. They surf one outgoing page, leap into its curling edge, and arrive on the destination tray inside a perfectly folded paper pocket.
premises.hook: The floor arrives one sheet at a time.
premises.visible_action: Sheets emerge, curl, and stack; messenger slides along a page; one corner folds into a pocket that lands on a tray.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A moving obstacle can sometimes supply the route.
premises.gate: Use a fictional low-force paper dispenser, never a person inside a real printer or moving machine.

premises.title: The Button Garden Expedition
premises.premise: A thimble-sized gardener needs to plant one bright seed in a neglected button box, but the smooth button surfaces offer nowhere to root. They discover a thread-filled buttonhole, nest the seed in it, and grow a fictional thread-flower that ties the scattered buttons into a garden path.
premises.hook: Every island has holes. One is a home.
premises.visible_action: Buttons tilt like islands; seed slides off polished surfaces; it settles in a threaded hole; yarn petals unfurl.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A feature that looks like a gap can become the useful place.
premises.gate: The seed and thread-flower are magical; not a horticultural claim or child-safe craft instruction.

premises.title: The Library Shelf Migration
premises.premise: A tiny librarian must move a paper village before a borrowed book leaves the shelf, but every house is stuck to a different page. They fold the houses flat, load them into the book’s bookmark, and unfurl the village on the neighboring volume just before the book is lifted.
premises.hook: Our entire town is due back today.
premises.visible_action: Paper roofs collapse; houses slide into a wide bookmark; bookmark bridges a gap; village pops open on a second spine.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Portability can be designed into a home for a story.
premises.gate: Use fictional books and paper inhabitants; avoid damaging real library property in any practical adaptation.

premises.title: The Teacup Lighthouse
premises.premise: A tiny sailor wants to guide a lost toy boat across a dark tabletop puddle, but reflections make three identical cup handles look like harbor entrances. The sailor rotates a patterned saucer under one cup, creating a distinctive moving reflection that the boat follows home.
premises.hook: Three harbors. Only one is real.
premises.visible_action: Boat circles reflected handles; saucer rotates; striped reflection sweeps the puddle; the boat follows the unique signal.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Distinctive signals can distinguish otherwise similar landmarks.
premises.gate: Stylized tabletop reflections; do not present as maritime navigation guidance.

premises.title: The Pencil-Shaving Spiral
premises.premise: A miniature courier must climb to a desk shelf after the ladder is removed. A curled pencil shaving keeps springing open underfoot, so the courier winds it around a thick marker to make a spiral path, delivers the parcel, and leaves the new path for the next traveler.
premises.hook: The only staircase is trying to uncurl.
premises.visible_action: Wood curl flexes; courier wraps it around a marker; a spiral walkway forms; parcel moves upward step by step.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A support can turn a floppy material into a usable shape.
premises.gate: Impossible miniature loads; no recommendation to make a load-bearing structure from pencil shavings.

premises.title: The Sock-Drawer Northern Lights
premises.premise: A tiny explorer seeks a colorful glow at the back of a sock drawer, but every opening floods the scene with harsh light and rearranges the terrain. They mark a path with paired socks, wait for the drawer to settle, and find an original glow-in-the-dark star patch casting the mysterious colors.
premises.hook: The sky changes every time the drawer opens.
premises.visible_action: Drawer slides; sock hills tumble gently; paired-sock markers align; a stitched star patch reveals its glow in the dark.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A mystery can have a small, local source.
premises.gate: Glow colors and scale are stylized; avoid implying that ordinary fabric produces light.

premises.title: The Record-Groove Express
premises.premise: A toy traveler must reach a label at the center of a slowly turning oversized record, but walking straight keeps carrying them sideways. They ride a fictional groove-following sled inward, step onto the stationary display spindle platform, and discover the parcel was a tiny dance invitation.
premises.hook: The road goes around. The address is in the middle.
premises.visible_action: Record turns slowly; footsteps arc; a sled follows an inward spiral; traveler dismounts at a fixed center platform.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A route can follow the landscape instead of fighting it.
premises.gate: Use an invented oversized display model, not a real turntable; do not claim actual record grooves form a practical ride.

premises.title: The Umbrella-Rib Observatory
premises.premise: A tiny astronomer wants to chart a pretend night sky inside an open umbrella, but each attempt to climb shifts the canopy and hides another star sticker. They lie flat in a suspended paper hammock between two ribs and finally see the full constellation, which outlines their missing hat.
premises.hook: The universe is the inside of an umbrella.
premises.visible_action: Canopy tilts; star stickers slide out of view; paper hammock swings into the center; constellation lines reveal a hat shape.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A different viewpoint can expose the whole pattern.
premises.gate: Invented constellation and miniature umbrella rig; not an astronomy identification lesson or real climbing apparatus.

premises.title: The Staircase That Unpacks Itself
premises.premise: A cubic traveler needs to reach a platform, but the staircase is stored as a compact accordion tower. Pulling a clearly marked top tab releases sequential hinges, and each unfolding tread frees the next until a walkable stair reaches the platform; the final step unfolds into a welcome mat.
premises.hook: The stairs are still in their box.
premises.visible_action: Top tab slides; hinged block pairs rotate in sequence; treads land on supports; last panel flips into a mat.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Sequenced dependencies can make a compact object deploy in order.
premises.gate: Fictional low-force hinges; no engineering claim about real load-bearing stairs.

premises.title: The Rain-Sorting Rooftops
premises.premise: A block village wants to fill three decorative ponds, but one roof sends all toy rain beads into the first basin. As each basin reaches its marked level, a floating block tips a channel toward the next, ending with a row of tiny flags instead of an overflowing plaza.
premises.hook: Every drop keeps choosing the same address.
premises.visible_action: Beads roll down roofs; floats rise; channels tilt one after another; three ponds fill to marks; flags lift.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A sequence can redirect a flow when each stage is ready.
premises.gate: Toy beads stand in for rain; model the mechanism consistently and avoid flood-control or water-safety claims.

premises.title: The Festival of Falling Curtains
premises.premise: A block troupe needs to reveal five stage scenes in order, but all curtains are tangled on one shared rail. They separate the rail into staggered tracks so each lowered curtain exposes the release tab for the next, revealing a traveling story whose final scene is the waiting audience.
premises.hook: Pull one curtain. Reveal the next job.
premises.visible_action: Block curtains slide down separate tracks; hidden tabs appear sequentially; five dioramas open; last mirror-like panel reflects simplified audience figures.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Reveal only the next actionable step when order matters.
premises.gate: Miniature fictional stage system; not a real overhead rigging plan.

premises.title: The Ice-Cube Post Office
premises.premise: A square courier must send three sealed parcels across a model ice shelf, but a single frozen conveyor is locked. Warm-colored fantasy tiles thaw one latch at a time, letting the conveyor advance in short sections until the parcels reach insulated nests and the courier receives a thank-you snowflake.
premises.hook: The mail route has frozen mid-sentence.
premises.visible_action: Glow tiles light in sequence; transparent latches soften; belt sections advance; parcels settle into nests; a snowflake card unfolds.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A stalled process can be restarted section by section.
premises.gate: Explicit fantasy thaw tiles; no claim about real ice melting rates, refrigeration, or mail handling.

premises.title: The Block City Night Wave
premises.premise: A caretaker wants to dim a toy city at bedtime, but the control is on a roof across the map. A prearranged sequence of mechanical shutters closes one window and exposes a reflector to the next, carrying a visible dimming wave across the city while leaving a moonlit path home.
premises.hook: Bedtime is crossing town one window at a time.
premises.visible_action: Shutters descend; tiny reflectors rotate; the next latch releases; lighted windows fade along a serpentine route; a path remains lit.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A sequence can carry a signal while preserving one needed exception.
premises.gate: Use an internally defined optical-mechanical toy rule; not real electrical or building-safety guidance.

premises.title: The Returning Picnic Table
premises.premise: A block family needs a picnic table on a bare square, but every piece is stored beneath a different paving tile. Opening the first compartment raises a leg that unlocks the next compartment; the final tabletop rotates into place, and the now-empty compartments become matching seats.
premises.hook: The park is hiding our lunch furniture.
premises.visible_action: Ground tiles flip; legs rise and latch; a tabletop rotates; remaining cavities lift seat blocks to ground level.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A deployment sequence can give emptied spaces a second purpose.
premises.gate: Clearly a toy world; no safe real furniture specification is implied.

premises.title: The Dandelion Launch Network
premises.premise: A block gardener wants to scatter square fantasy seeds across an empty grid, but one launcher keeps dropping them in a pile. Landing seeds depress miniature release platforms for preloaded launchers farther away, spreading a bounded zigzag trail until the final seed raises a miniature garden sign.
premises.hook: The first seed has to start the next journey.
premises.visible_action: Seed cubes arc between soft platforms; platforms dip; preloaded cartoon arms release in sequence; a zigzag planting pattern fills the grid.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A chain can distribute outputs instead of piling them at its start.
premises.gate: Fantasy block seeds and preloaded low-force toy launchers; show finite stored energy, not perpetual motion. No ecology, germination, or weapon-building claims.

premises.title: The Spiral Library Return
premises.premise: A block librarian wants to return a ring of oversized books to shelves, but the aisle is too narrow for a cart. Each shelving tray rotates into an empty position and frees the next tray, circulating one vacancy around the ring until all books land beside their matching symbols.
premises.hook: We only have one empty space.
premises.visible_action: One empty tray rotates; books travel in a ring; shelf symbols line up; the vacancy returns to its original bay.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: An empty position can be a useful resource in a constrained sequence.
premises.gate: Fictional rotating shelf model; validate every intermediate clearance before rendering the mechanism.

premises.title: The Kite That Rebuilt the Skyline
premises.premise: A cubic festival organizer must raise a skyline-shaped banner, but the folded display lies in a heap. A tethered fantasy kite pulls a guided cable through successive counterweighted facades, raising each panel to its stop until their shadows spell the festival’s invented name.
premises.hook: The skyline is packed flat. The kite is clocking in.
premises.visible_action: Kite climbs on a fixed path; cable runs through visible guides; facades pivot upright in sequence; their shadows align into letters.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: The order of assembly can be part of the spectacle.
premises.gate: Toy fantasy kite and architecture; no real rigging, aviation, or load-bearing instruction.

premises.title: The Marble Museum Tour
premises.premise: A block curator needs one glowing marble to illuminate a series of exhibits, but the last room is unreachable by the original track. Each arriving marble activates a turntable that aligns the next track segment, and the final turntable routes it back through the ceiling as the museum’s glowing exit sign.
premises.hook: One marble. Every exhibit gets a moment.
premises.visible_action: Marble rolls through lit display bays; turntables rotate between fixed stops; a final ramp rises; marble rests inside EXIT letters.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A route can change its configuration as a traveler advances.
premises.gate: Fictional mechanism with explicit energy sources and ramp geometry required in production; no perpetual-motion implication.

premises.title: The Three-Lamp Switch Dance
premises.premise: A toy technician must turn three dark lamps on. Left toggles lamps 1 and 2, middle toggles 2 and 3, and right toggles 1 only; after noisy guesswork, the technician presses middle then right, lighting all three in exactly two presses and revealing a tiny stage.
premises.hook: Two presses. Three lamps. Which two?
premises.visible_action: Labeled switches depress; lamp states flip; a two-row state diagram appears; middle then right produces three lit bulbs.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Track the state changes rather than the switch names.
premises.gate: Verified from initial state 000: middle gives 011 and right gives 111; no single available switch lights all three. Show these exact toggle rules.

premises.title: The Lift to Floor Seven
premises.premise: A toy lift starts at floor 0 and must reach floor 7 using a +3 button and a -2 button, without leaving floors 0 through 9. The operator tries four moves in the order +3, +3, -2, +3, yielding 0, 3, 6, 4, 7; the lift opens to a tiny rooftop garden.
premises.hook: Up three. Down two. Can we land on seven?
premises.visible_action: Floor display changes 0 to 3 to 6 to 4 to 7; an on-screen path traces four presses; garden panels unfold.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Write the actual sequence before calling a route impossible.
premises.gate: Verified four-press route. Equation 3u-2d=7 has shortest nonnegative solution u=3,d=1; all listed floors stay within bounds.

premises.title: The Token Ferry
premises.premise: Three round tokens need to cross a model gap in a ferry that carries at most two. A token must ride the ferry on every trip; after overfilling fails, two cross, one returns, and the last pair crosses, leaving all three at the far platform in three trips.
premises.hook: The boat needs a passenger, even coming back.
premises.visible_action: Two tokens board; ferry glides right; one token rides back; the remaining pair travels right; three tokens line up at the destination.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Count the return trip as part of the plan.
premises.gate: Verified three-trip schedule for three tokens, capacity two, and at least one rider per trip. This is a toy state puzzle, not real boating advice.

premises.title: The Five-Block Balance
premises.premise: A maker must place blocks of weights 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 on a toy balance while leaving exactly one block unused. They set 1+5 opposite 2+4, leaving 3 as the prize pedestal; both sides total 6 and the final block displays the answer.
premises.hook: Use four blocks. Leave one out. Make it level.
premises.visible_action: Numbered blocks move between pans; totals appear; 1 and 5 settle opposite 2 and 4; unused 3 rises as a pedestal.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Equal totals can come from different combinations.
premises.gate: Verified 1+5=2+4=6 with one unused block. Present this as one valid solution, not the only solution; ideal equal-arm balance model.

premises.title: The One-Cell Traffic Jam
premises.premise: Three labeled tiles A, B, C occupy slots 1, 2, 3 on a four-position ring with slot 4 empty. A caretaker must move A to slot 2 while retaining clockwise tile order; C slides to 4, B to 3, and A to 2, leaving the vacancy at slot 1 without any tile passing another.
premises.hook: Nobody can pass. One space can travel.
premises.visible_action: C slides from 3 to 4; B slides from 2 to 3; A slides from 1 to 2; the empty slot finishes at 1.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Moving the empty space can move the whole arrangement.
premises.gate: Use exactly the verified adjacent sequence C:3→4, B:2→3, A:1→2. The tiles preserve their cyclic order; no swapping or hidden lift is allowed.

premises.title: Two Reversals Make a Return
premises.premise: A stage mechanic wants a pointer to turn clockwise, but two meshed toy gears reverse the input direction. They insert a third gear between input and pointer, turn the input clockwise, and watch the pointer rotate clockwise too, landing on a tiny applause sign.
premises.hook: Why is the pointer going the wrong way?
premises.visible_action: Two gears mesh and turn oppositely; a center idler slides into a new spaced layout; three gear arrows alternate directions.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Count each reversal in a simple gear train.
premises.gate: Verified external spur-gear direction parity: two meshes preserve input direction. Gear centers, compatible tooth pitch, and clearances must be consistent; this is a simplified gear-train model, not a fabrication guide.

premises.title: The Two-Weight Elevator
premises.premise: A puppet needs to lower a toy platform gently, but the two removable counterweight blocks together outweigh it and one alone underbalances it in the simplified model. The puppet transfers a small labeled trim block to the platform, brings the stated totals into balance, and uses a visible hand crank for controlled movement.
premises.hook: The lift keeps choosing a side.
premises.visible_action: Numbered weights hang from a visible cable; totals compare; trim block moves; crank rotates; platform descends one marked stop.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A balance condition and a motion-control mechanism are separate questions.
premises.gate: Define all masses and friction if used educationally; no numerical answer is asserted here. Not a real elevator, hoist, or suspended-load construction guide.

premises.title: The Spiral Lock That Shows Its Work
premises.premise: A keeper must release a toy treasure tray using three concentric rings, but random turns keep hiding the exit slot. A cutaway reveals that every ring needs its notch at the top; the keeper aligns the outer, middle, and inner notches and slides out a single celebratory biscuit.
premises.hook: The lock is not guessing. We are.
premises.visible_action: Opaque cover becomes transparent; three notches rotate independently to a top marker; a straight pin lifts; tray slides forward.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Make the hidden condition visible before trying more moves.
premises.gate: Invented toy notch puzzle, not a real security-device bypass; production must show a consistent pin path and independent ring motion.

premises.title: The Nine-Tile Mosaic
premises.premise: An artist must fill a 3-by-3 board with nine tiles so each row shows one circle, one square, and one triangle. The first attempt repeats a circle; they rearrange rows as circle-square-triangle, square-triangle-circle, triangle-circle-square, producing rows and columns with one of each.
premises.hook: Every row wants all three shapes.
premises.visible_action: Tiles slide into nine cells; duplicate symbols flash; rows rotate into a Latin-square pattern; matching columns illuminate.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Check constraints in both directions when the puzzle promises both.
premises.gate: Verified 3×3 Latin square; each row and column contains C,S,T exactly once. If only rows are required, the displayed answer is valid but not unique.

premises.title: The Finite Spring Finale
premises.premise: A maker wants a toy theater to run forever on one wound spring, but the scene slows after each cycle. A cutaway shows the finite winding unwinding; the maker adds a visible audience hand crank and relabels the show HELP KEEP IT GOING, turning failure into participation.
premises.hook: The machine works forever. Until now.
premises.visible_action: Spring unwinds; stage carousel slows; winding indicator reaches zero; an external crank appears; audience turns it and the scene resumes.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Show the input that keeps a mechanism moving.
premises.gate: The energy-accounting lesson requires primary physics-source review before publication. Avoid numerical efficiency claims or treating this stylized model as a validated device.

premises.title: The Missing Circle Is a Hole
premises.premise: A museum guard must find the circle stolen from a three-shape display, but every search focuses on loose objects. Turning on a lamp reveals that the circle is the empty hole between two curved display pieces; the guard hangs the FOUND label around the gap.
premises.hook: We found every object. Where is the circle?
premises.visible_action: Guard lifts a square and triangle, searches behind plinths, shifts a lamp, and frames the circular negative space with a label.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Look at the spaces between objects as well as the objects.
premises.gate: Verify that the final silhouette is genuinely circular in the rendered view; no general claim about visual perception performance.

premises.title: The Giant Footprint Close-Up
premises.premise: A scout wants to identify a supposed giant after discovering an enormous three-toed print, but every proposed monster contradicts the next clue. The camera finally pulls back to show a tiny scout examining the end of a garden fork pressed into clay, and the scout updates the sketch to FORK.
premises.hook: Whatever made this has three terrible toes.
premises.visible_action: Scout measures the print; monster doodles grow; camera pulls back; a fork-shaped tool rests beside the matching clay impression.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Scale and framing can change an interpretation.
premises.gate: Use a toy fork and clay model; the reveal must match the footprint geometry exactly.

premises.title: The Camouflage Coat Check
premises.premise: A coat-check attendant must find a customer’s checkerboard coat, but it vanishes against the identical wall pattern. Instead of repainting anything, the attendant slides a plain screen behind the rack and every coat becomes visible; the customer had also blended into the opposite wall.
premises.hook: Your coat is here. So are you. Probably.
premises.visible_action: Patterned coats overlap the wall; a blank screen travels behind the rack; silhouettes emerge; customer steps away from another matching pattern.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Changing the background can reveal the subject.
premises.gate: Demonstrate only the specific rendered contrast; do not claim universal camouflage or accessibility results.

premises.title: The Shadow With an Extra Arm
premises.premise: A stagehand must find a supposed extra performer shown in a wall shadow, but the cast count is correct. A side view reveals that a coat-rack branch overlaps one actor’s shadow; moving the rack separates the silhouettes and gives the branch its own tiny bow.
premises.hook: We hired three people. The wall hired four.
premises.visible_action: Three actors pose; an extra shadow arm waves as a rack rolls; side view exposes overlap; rack moves away and shadows separate.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: One silhouette can combine several separate sources.
premises.gate: Check actual lamp and object positions so the reveal explains the visible shadow without a continuity cheat.

premises.title: The Treasure Beneath the Caption
premises.premise: A treasure hunter searches a minimalist stage for a tiny key, but every explanatory caption lands directly over it. The hunter grabs the floating SEARCH HERE text and moves it aside, revealing the key; the final label reads MAYBE LESS TEXT and stays safely in the corner.
premises.hook: The clue is being covered by the clue.
premises.visible_action: Hunter circles stage; captions bounce onto the key; text is dragged upward; key glints; final label shrinks into a corner.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Explanations can obstruct the thing they explain.
premises.gate: Make the hidden key present from the opening frame; do not falsely imply a missing object was visible earlier.

premises.title: The Four Rotations Portrait
premises.premise: A courier must identify a face on an oddly arranged tile, but it looks like scattered marks at first. They rotate the same tile by quarter turns; at the third orientation two marks read as eyes and a curve as a smile, matching the recipient, who has been standing sideways beside them.
premises.hook: The address is a face with the wrong way up.
premises.visible_action: One unchanged tile rotates in 90-degree steps; marks settle into a face; camera reveals recipient leaning sideways; both straighten.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Orientation can make an intended pattern easier to recognize.
premises.gate: Keep mark positions unchanged across all rotations and use an original simple face; no claim about face-recognition science.

premises.title: The Ten Squares in the Window
premises.premise: A window cleaner must count every square in a 2-by-2 square window, but the label demanding TEN is wrong. They outline the four small squares and the single large square, replace TEN with FIVE, and reveal that the boss had accidentally counted the same window’s reflection too.
premises.hook: The sign says ten. Count the glass yourself.
premises.visible_action: Four cell outlines flash; the outer frame highlights; five counters appear; a reflected duplicate slides into view; incorrect sign is corrected.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Check what is being counted, including duplicates and larger shapes.
premises.gate: A 2×2 grid contains 4 unit squares plus 1 size-2 square, total 5. Reflection creates a second image, not five additional physical window squares; title is intentionally the mistaken claim.

premises.title: The Vanishing Stripe Train
premises.premise: A miniature detective wants to find which of three stationary striped boxes contains a toy train, but all look flat against striped scenery. They move a small viewing window sideways; parallax exposes the near box’s raised wheels, and the train rolls out only after being correctly identified.
premises.hook: Nothing is moving. So why did that stripe shift?
premises.visible_action: Viewing aperture slides; foreground stripe edges shift relative to the background; tiny wheels emerge; one box unfolds into a toy train.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Changing viewpoint can reveal depth hidden in one view.
premises.gate: Parallax must be physically consistent in the scene; avoid claims about diagnosing vision or universal human perception.

premises.title: The Lost Star in the Dance
premises.premise: A choreographer must find a star badge among five moving dancers, but rapid position swaps make guessing unreliable. They pause the formation at each beat and track the badge-bearing dancer by a distinct square shoe, then reveal that the star was always pinned on that dancer’s back.
premises.hook: Follow the shoe, not the sparkle.
premises.visible_action: Five figures swap marked positions; square shoe remains consistent; freeze frames show the path; final dancer turns to expose the badge.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Use a stable identifier when positions keep changing.
premises.gate: Maintain identity and badge continuity in every frame; present as this specific tracking puzzle, not a test of intelligence or attention.

premises.title: The Arrow That Was a Fish
premises.premise: A traveler follows a painted arrow through a gallery, but it repeatedly appears to point back toward the entrance. Walking around the freestanding sculpture reveals that the supposed arrow is a flat fish silhouette viewed end-on; a separate clearly labeled route sign finally leads to the exhibit.
premises.hook: The directions have a tail.
premises.visible_action: Camera orbits a narrow sculptural profile; arrowhead becomes a fish fin; body widens; traveler spots the real route marker.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Check whether an apparent instruction is actually a sign.
premises.gate: Design and verify the exact camera-dependent silhouette; do not rely on changing the sculpture between shots.

premises.title: The Empty Seat Sketch
premises.premise: A sketch artist wants to draw a two-person picnic, but the second seat stays empty and every attempt to erase it leaves a mark. They turn the mark into a flower growing beside the seat and finish a drawing that has room for both absence and today’s sunshine.
premises.hook: The seat stays.
premises.visible_action: Pencil traces two chairs; eraser rubs one pale mark; a stem grows from it; artist colors a small flower and closes the sketchbook gently.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A picture can hold an absence without hiding it.
premises.gate: Treat the absent person’s reason as unspecified; do not claim that a creative act resolves grief or mental-health needs.

premises.title: The Umbrella Left Open
premises.premise: A figure wants to hurry home after rain, but notices a shivering paper bird beneath a dripping bench. They leave their umbrella open as a shelter and walk away; the next morning a neat row of paper feathers marks the route to the returned umbrella.
premises.hook: Someone still needs the shelter.
premises.visible_action: Figure stops mid-stride; umbrella lowers over bird; footsteps leave; morning feathers lead back to a dry folded umbrella.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A small kindness can be shown without a speech.
premises.gate: The paper bird is a fictional creature; no wildlife rescue or animal-care instructions.

premises.title: The Line Across Two Windows
premises.premise: Two neighbors want company without interrupting each other’s quiet evenings. One draws a small hill on a window, the other continues the line on theirs, and over several nights the separate drawings become one landscape that both sit beside with their lights on.
premises.hook: One line reaches the next window.
premises.visible_action: A curved line appears on one pane; another extends it; mountains, a river, and two tiny houses gradually connect across the building gap.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Connection can be gentle and leave room for quiet.
premises.gate: Use fictional neighbors and transparent removable drawing materials; no implied obligation to socialize.

premises.title: The Scuffed Dance Floor
premises.premise: A dancer wants to perform on a spotless floor and keeps wiping away every rehearsal mark. When the cloth becomes worn out, they step back and notice the remaining marks trace the dance; they leave the path visible and perform along it for one quiet spectator.
premises.hook: The floor remembers every attempt.
premises.visible_action: Feet draw scuff arcs; cloth erases sections; an overhead shot reveals a winding route; dancer follows it into a final still pose.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Traces of practice can belong in the finished work.
premises.gate: Fictional expressive movement; not advice to dance on slippery, damaged, or unsafe flooring.

premises.title: The Tiny Birthday Candle
premises.premise: A figure plans a grand birthday display but only one small candle arrives. They arrange empty chairs in disappointment, then friends enter carrying single tiny lights of their own, forming a constellation around the modest cake without changing its size.
premises.hook: One little light is already here.
premises.visible_action: Large empty display outline fades; one light flickers; friends place cold glowing dots around a cake; overhead view forms a constellation.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: The scale of a gathering is not the scale of its care.
premises.gate: Use flameless fantasy lights; avoid equating social attendance with personal worth.

premises.title: The Raincoat Patch
premises.premise: A traveler wants to hide a conspicuous patch on an old raincoat, repeatedly folding it out of sight. A childlike paper puppet places a tiny matching patch on its own cloak, and the traveler lets the coat hang naturally before adding a playful second patch shaped like a cloud.
premises.hook: The patch can stay.
premises.visible_action: Coat folds inward; stitched patch peeks out; puppet applies a matching shape; traveler unfolds coat and adds a cloud patch.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A repair can become part of an object’s story.
premises.gate: A gentle fictional confidence story; do not frame clothing repair as a cure for shame or social anxiety.

premises.title: The Last Note on the Bench
premises.premise: A busker wants to finish a melody, but the single listener leaves before the final note. The busker plays it anyway; a folded paper bird left on the bench opens to show the listener’s drawing of the performance, and the busker places it beside the case.
premises.hook: The final note still belongs here.
premises.visible_action: Listener rises and exits; musician hesitates then plays; paper bird unfolds; drawing catches a small pool of light.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A moment can matter even when its ending is quiet.
premises.gate: Use an original melody and original drawing; do not infer a stranger’s feelings beyond the visible fictional gesture.

premises.title: The Plant That Leaned Toward Two Desks
premises.premise: Two quiet office neighbors both try to place a shared decorative paper plant nearer the other as a gift, sliding it back and forth overnight. They finally push their desks into an L shape and set the plant at the shared corner, where its two paper branches point toward both seats.
premises.hook: It was meant for you.
premises.visible_action: Plant slides left and right between cuts; two gift tags appear; desks rotate into an L; paper branches open toward both figures.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A gift does not always need a single owner.
premises.gate: Use a paper plant so its movement makes no unsupported claim about plant behavior.

premises.title: The Pocket-Sized Home
premises.premise: A traveler wants to unpack in a bare temporary room, but the oversized suitcase makes every object feel out of place. They find one small familiar drawing in a side pocket, tape it beside the bed, and gradually arrange the room around that single recognizable corner.
premises.hook: Start with one familiar corner.
premises.visible_action: Suitcase opens over empty floor; objects hover indecisively; a small drawing is placed; lamp, cup, and blanket settle nearby.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: One familiar detail can be a starting point for a new space.
premises.gate: Keep the circumstances of temporary housing unspecified; no claim that decoration resolves displacement or hardship.

premises.title: The Kite String That Stayed
premises.premise: Two friends want to keep flying a kite together, but one must leave before the breeze ends. They tie a tiny ribbon at the last shared grip point; the remaining friend flies the kite from below the ribbon and later wraps the spool with both names before putting it away.
premises.hook: There is still a place for your hand.
premises.visible_action: Two hands hold a spool; one releases; ribbon is tied; kite arcs gently; spool winds shut with ribbon visible on top.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A small marker can preserve a shared moment.
premises.gate: Use toy-scale open terrain and avoid real kite safety advice; separation is ordinary and not explained as a crisis.

premises.title: The Draft That Ate the Deadline
premises.premise: An animator wants to finish a short scene, but each new idea physically adds another page to a growing paper creature. They choose one page with the clearest action, park the rest in a labeled NEXT TIME box, and finish the scene while the creature curls up for a nap.
premises.hook: The draft has grown legs.
premises.visible_action: Pages sprout limbs and sprawl across a desk; animator extracts one page; remaining sheets fold into a box; final shot plays on a tiny screen.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Choosing what to finish can matter more than generating more options.
premises.gate: Metaphorical creative process; do not promise productivity outcomes from a single technique.

premises.title: The Placeholder King
premises.premise: A designer wants to polish a title card but keeps treating a temporary gray rectangle as the final centerpiece. When the placeholder begins issuing absurd royal orders, the designer labels it TEMP, shrinks it to a corner, and finally draws the actual scene it was meant to support.
premises.hook: The placeholder has taken over the project.
premises.visible_action: Gray rectangle gains a paper crown; layout elements bow; TEMP stamp lands; rectangle shrinks; original scene expands behind it.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Make temporary decisions visibly temporary.
premises.gate: Original fictional characters and rules; do not present the gag as an empirical claim.

premises.title: The Eraser’s Overtime
premises.premise: An illustrator wants a clean first line and erases every stroke until the paper becomes a transparent window. Looking through the hole reveals the messy sketch beneath, which already contains the desired pose; they trace only its strongest contour and let the rest stay loose.
premises.hook: The eraser has done more work than the pencil.
premises.visible_action: Pencil touches down; eraser scrubs; paper thins; lower sketch appears; one decisive contour closes around a pose.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: An imperfect attempt may contain the part you need.
premises.gate: Magical paper erosion, no literal instruction to damage materials; not a universal creative method claim.

premises.title: The Soundtrack Before the Footstep
premises.premise: A filmmaker wants an impressive soundtrack but keeps adding epic music to a scene where the character only takes one ordinary step. They mute the score, refine the footstep timing, and bring back one perfectly timed tiny percussion hit that makes the simple action funny.
premises.hook: The music is saving the world. He is crossing a rug.
premises.visible_action: Orchestra symbols flood the frame; figure takes a tiny step; volume sliders drop; heel lands with one small sound mark.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Match emphasis to what the scene actually does.
premises.gate: Use original audio; the payoff is an editorial choice rather than a claim about universally effective comedy.

premises.title: The Reference Pile Avalanche
premises.premise: A maker wants to build one original toy creature, but reference cards pile so high that the workbench disappears. They select three abstract requirements from the pile, such as rolls, folds, and glows, put the cards aside, and build an original folding wheel-creature from those constraints.
premises.hook: I can see every reference except my own idea.
premises.visible_action: Cards stack into a wall; three verbs remain on tabs; maker clears a small workspace; a new wheel-creature unfolds and lights up.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Translate references into requirements rather than copying their surfaces.
premises.gate: All shown reference cards must be original generic sketches; no reproduction or style imitation of established characters.

premises.title: The Progress Bar Painter
premises.premise: A painter wants a progress meter for a mural, but keeps painting the meter itself until the bar reaches 100 percent beside an empty wall. They relabel it METER COMPLETE, laugh, and replace it with small checkboxes for actual mural sections, finishing one visible section before the cut.
premises.hook: One hundred percent of what?
premises.visible_action: Progress bar fills; camera reveals untouched wall; label changes; three task boxes appear; one section is painted and one box checked.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Measure the work you mean to complete.
premises.gate: Fictional workflow metaphor; no general claim that checklists guarantee project completion.

premises.title: The Camera That Would Not Sit Still
premises.premise: An animator wants a dramatic reveal but keeps orbiting the camera so quickly that the small character’s important gesture is invisible. They lock the camera for one clean shot, let the gesture finish, and reserve one slow move for the actual reveal of a huge birthday sign behind the character.
premises.hook: The camera is doing all the acting.
premises.visible_action: Camera-path rings spin around a still figure; motion freezes; hands complete a tiny action; one deliberate dolly reveals the sign.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Give the viewer time to read the action.
premises.gate: Editorial demonstration with original scene; avoid medical claims about motion sensitivity or attention.

premises.title: The Font Committee
premises.premise: A creator wants one readable caption, but each letter insists on using a different decorative costume. After the words become impossible to fit, the creator gives every letter the same simple outfit and lets only the key word wear a small hat, making the joke readable at a glance.
premises.hook: Every letter wants the leading role.
premises.visible_action: Letters arrive in ornate costumes, bump off the line, change into simple forms, and settle; one key word gains a tiny hat.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Hierarchy can give a detail emphasis without decorating everything.
premises.gate: Use original letterforms or licensed fonts; test actual readability rather than claiming universal accessibility.

premises.title: The Render Queue Picnic
premises.premise: A creator wants to use a waiting period well but keeps refreshing an animated render meter, causing their imaginary chair to grow roots. They place a visible notification bell beside the screen, prepare a tiny picnic on the desk, and return when the completed frame appears as the picnic’s final placemat.
premises.hook: Refresh. Refresh. Still a sandwich-sized wait.
premises.visible_action: Refresh icon spins; chair sprouts cartoon roots; bell is set; food-shaped paper props unfold; bell rings and completed image slides out.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A waiting process can have a clear return signal.
premises.gate: The render result is part of the fiction; do not imply any real render has been run or predict real processing time.

premises.title: The Sequel Before Scene One
premises.premise: A storyteller wants to launch a ten-part saga, but every unfinished first scene splits into more sequel posters. They fold the posters into a small screening room, finish a self-contained first scene, and let the single audience member choose whether another poster comes down from storage.
premises.hook: Episode twelve is ready. Episode one is a rectangle.
premises.visible_action: Posters multiply along a wall; first-scene rectangle remains blank; posters fold into seats; one short scene plays; audience points at one future poster.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A complete small story can support what comes next.
premises.gate: Use entirely original poster art; no claim that this approach guarantees audience growth.

premises.title: The Mug Handle Treaty
premises.premise: Two people sharing a tiny table both keep rotating a mug handle into the other’s workspace. They mark a small neutral landing spot between their notebooks, place the mug there after each sip, and discover the table finally has room for a biscuit plate too.
premises.hook: The handle has crossed the border again.
premises.visible_action: Mug rotates; pens are nudged; two notebooks slide; a circle is drawn on a coaster; mug returns to center; biscuit plate enters.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A small agreed place can end repeated friction.
premises.gate: Original fictional characters and rules; do not present the gag as an empirical claim.

premises.title: The Laundry Label Mystery
premises.premise: A figure wants to pair socks from a basket, but every sock carries a confusing abstract tag. Instead of deciphering the tags, they lay the socks heel-to-heel and compare shape and length, making pairs; the final unmatched sock becomes a puppet who proudly introduces the basket.
premises.hook: Every sock has a label. None of them help.
premises.visible_action: Tags flap; socks fan across the floor; heels align; pairs fold together; lone sock rises as a speaking puppet.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Use the features that actually answer the immediate question.
premises.gate: This is a matching gag, not care-label or textile-cleaning advice.

premises.title: The Shopping List Origami
premises.premise: A shopper wants to remember three ordinary items, but their overfolded paper list has hidden each word behind another crease. They unfold it into an absurdly large paper shape, copy the three items onto one small clear card, and use the original as a bag-shaped prop for the walk home.
premises.hook: I made the list portable and the words inaccessible.
premises.visible_action: Folded paper rotates through many shapes; three words appear separately; a plain card is written; old list folds into a decorative bag shape.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Compression is useful only if the information stays accessible.
premises.gate: The folded paper bag is a stylized prop, not a claim that it can safely carry groceries.

premises.title: The Elevator Button Courtesy Loop
premises.premise: Two neighbors each insist the other should choose the destination first, leaving a toy lift motionless through an elaborate polite exchange. One draws two floor numbers on a card, both point to the same number, and they press it together before bowing themselves almost out of the frame.
premises.hook: After you. After you. Still after you.
premises.visible_action: Hands hover over buttons; bows deepen; card appears; two fingers land on the same number; lift display finally changes.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A tiny explicit choice can resolve excessive politeness.
premises.gate: Fictional lift interaction; no operational or emergency elevator advice.

premises.title: The Perfectly Timed Toast
premises.premise: A figure wants butter and toast ready together, but repeatedly prepares one long before the other in an exaggerated kitchen ballet. They arrange the plate, spreader, and butter first, then wait for the toaster’s normal finish signal and assemble one calm breakfast before sitting down.
premises.hook: The toast is ready. The breakfast is not.
premises.visible_action: Plate slides late; butter crosses the room; tools collide harmlessly; a simple three-item setup appears; toast pops and is plated.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Prepare the nearby steps before the time-sensitive step ends.
premises.gate: Keep appliances normally used and hands away from slots; no cooking-temperature or food-safety claims.

premises.title: The Key That Lived in the Other Pocket
premises.premise: A commuter wants to leave on time, but searches the same jacket pocket after every distraction. They empty both pockets onto two labeled circles, spot the key under a folded note, and choose a single small tray by the exit for its return that evening.
premises.hook: I checked that pocket. I checked that pocket again.
premises.visible_action: Hands revisit one pocket; objects tumble into two circles; note unfolds and exposes key; evening cut shows key landing in a tray.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Make a repeated search visible and give the item a repeatable home.
premises.gate: A fictional organization choice, not a guarantee about memory or attention.

premises.title: The Plant-Watering Calendar Duel
premises.premise: Two roommates each think the other forgot to water a decorative paper plant and add blue paper droplets to its pot. The absurd droplet pile reveals the duplicated effort; they put one reversible DONE card beside the pot and take turns flipping it as part of a pretend care routine.
premises.hook: We both remembered. That is the problem.
premises.visible_action: Blue paper droplets accumulate; pot bulges with confetti; roommates compare calendars; one two-sided card flips and droplets stop doubling.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Make a shared task’s status visible to both people.
premises.gate: Use a clearly artificial plant and paper water; no real plant watering frequency or care advice.

premises.title: The Blanket Border Negotiation
premises.premise: Two friends watching a film keep tugging one square blanket toward themselves, exposing the other’s feet. They rotate it diagonally and sit closer to the same corner, then notice the sleeping toy pet has quietly claimed the warmest center fold.
premises.hook: The blanket treaty has collapsed again.
premises.visible_action: Blanket shifts left and right; toes appear; blanket rotates to a diamond; friends settle at adjacent corners; toy pet peeks from the center.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Try a new arrangement before repeating the same tug-of-war.
premises.gate: Specific fictional blanket proportions; do not imply diagonal rotation always provides more usable coverage.

premises.title: The Queue Number on the Wrong Side
premises.premise: A customer wants to know when their turn arrives but keeps watching the decorative back of a ticket. Nearby numbers advance until they rotate the ticket, discover theirs was just called, and politely show the attendant; the attendant flips a sample ticket above the counter for the next confused customer.
premises.hook: My ticket seems very abstract.
premises.visible_action: Display increments; ticket shows only a swirl; customer flips it to reveal a number; attendant mounts a two-sided sample.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: An error can reveal where the interface needs a clearer cue.
premises.gate: Fictional service policy; do not imply a real business must honor a missed queue number.

premises.title: The One-Trip Grocery Pride
premises.premise: A shopper insists on carrying every empty prop bag in one trip, turning into a wobbling tower of handles. They set everything down, make two easy trips, and discover that the dramatic ONE TRIP badge can be folded into a useful shelf label reading TWO IS FINE.
premises.hook: One trip. Seventeen handles. A questionable victory.
premises.visible_action: Bag handles collect along arms; tower sways; bags are set down; two small loads cross the frame; badge folds into a label.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A self-imposed rule can be dropped when it makes the task worse.
premises.gate: Use visibly lightweight empty bags; no lifting limits, injury claims, or unsafe-load demonstration.

premises.title: The Moon’s Lost Appointment
premises.premise: A junior sky keeper must deliver a miniature moon to the evening sky, but the appointment card is written in shadows that disappear under the desk lamp. They read it by the moon’s own glow, find the correct slot, and slide the moon into place just as a paper owl clocks in.
premises.hook: The moon is late because its calendar is in shadow.
premises.visible_action: Desk lamp washes out dark marks; moon glow reveals them; a sky-panel slot opens; moon rises; owl-shaped clock flips to NIGHT.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Read a message under the conditions it was designed for.
premises.gate: All celestial mechanics and shadow-writing are explicit fantasy; not astronomy instruction.

premises.title: The Robot Who Collected Exceptions
premises.premise: A tidy robot wants to sort every object into square or round boxes, but a teardrop-shaped keepsake fits neither rule. Instead of cutting it to fit, the robot adds an EXCEPTIONS shelf, then finds that the shelf holds the most interesting objects in the room and gives each a small name tag.
premises.hook: This shape is not in my instructions.
premises.visible_action: Robot rotates keepsake against two box openings; cutting icon is crossed out; new shelf extends; odd shapes gather with individual labels.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A useful system can make room for things outside its first categories.
premises.gate: Fictional robot behavior; no assertion about actual AI capabilities, sentience, or classification fairness.

premises.title: The Planet With a Pause Button
premises.premise: A traveler needs to cross a tiny rotating planet to meet a friend, but pressing its pause button also freezes every helpful moving platform. They release pause, learn the visible platform rhythm, and ride the normal cycle around the globe while the friend holds up a patiently rotating welcome flag.
premises.hook: Pausing the problem paused the solution too.
premises.visible_action: Planet stops mid-rotation; stepping platforms freeze apart; button releases; traveler boards at a marked beat and circles to the friend.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A control can disable useful motion along with the obstacle.
premises.gate: Imaginary planetary control and physics; keep movement rules consistent within the story.

premises.title: The Dragon’s Paperwork Breeze
premises.premise: A tiny dragon wants a library card, but every nervous snort sends the forms flying. The librarian supplies one heavy reusable slate, the dragon writes by tracing soot with a claw, and its approved first loan is a picture book about taking one quiet breath.
premises.hook: Please complete the form without making it airborne.
premises.visible_action: Paper forms flutter; dragon blushes; slate lands; soot lines form simple letters; a small card slides across the desk.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Adapt the interface to the participant when possible.
premises.gate: Original dragon and books; fire and soot are magical cartoon effects, not an inhalation or writing-material recommendation.

premises.title: The Comet Tail Repair Shop
premises.premise: A mechanic must repair a comet’s tangled decorative tail before a parade, but brushing it straight removes every playful curl. They arrange the curls into a deliberate spiral ribbon, attach a tiny parade bell, and send the comet off with its unusual tail proudly intact.
premises.hook: Your tail is not broken. It is badly introduced.
premises.visible_action: Comet parks at a tiny bay; tail knots loosen; curls spring back; ribbon forms a spiral; comet glides away trailing the new pattern.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A repair can preserve character rather than erase it.
premises.gate: Personified decorative comet; no claim about real comet composition, trajectories, or repair.

premises.title: The Memory Cloud Weather Report
premises.premise: A cloud archivist wants to retrieve one happy picnic memory from a fantasy sky cabinet, but all the cloud drawers look identical. They sort the clouds by the objects visible inside instead of by cloud shape, find the red picnic kite, and label the drawer with that distinctive detail.
premises.hook: The forecast says scattered memories.
premises.visible_action: Cloud drawers drift; blurred mini-scenes swirl; archivist spots cup, umbrella, and kite icons; one drawer opens to an original picnic tableau.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A specific cue can organize a fictional collection better than a vague category.
premises.gate: Magical memory storage; no medical or scientific claim about human memory or recovery.

premises.title: The Time Machine With a Receipt
premises.premise: An inventor wants to recover a dropped biscuit by rewinding ten seconds, but each rewind also undoes the machine’s own setup. They write the lesson on an external fantasy receipt that persists across resets, then stop rewinding and place a plate beneath the biscuit’s next wobble.
premises.hook: Every retry forgets why we tried.
premises.visible_action: Clock hand spins backward; machine panels refold; receipt grows outside a glowing time boundary; inventor reads it and positions a plate.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A retry helps only if something learned survives it.
premises.gate: Explicit time-travel fantasy with a stated persistent-receipt exception; no actual time-travel claim.

premises.title: The Alien Who Bought a Reflection
premises.premise: An alien visitor wants to take home a shiny moon seen in a pond, but scooping the water keeps breaking the reflected image. A local artist paints a small original moon card; the alien trades a star-shaped pebble for it and holds the card still while the real reflection ripples goodbye.
premises.hook: I would like one moon, to go.
premises.visible_action: Scoop enters water; moon image fragments; alien looks puzzled; artist paints a card; card and pebble exchange; pond reflection reforms.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A representation can travel even when its source cannot.
premises.gate: Original alien design; stylized reflections should remain visually consistent, with no claim that the moon is physically in the pond.

premises.title: The Space Station’s Missing Down
premises.premise: A toy astronaut wants to hang a welcome sign, but in the fantasy station every visitor arrives from a different wall. They replace the one-direction sign with a slowly rotating ring of repeated WELCOME text, then add matching floor symbols so each arrival can orient to a chosen route.
premises.hook: Which way is the welcome upside down?
premises.visible_action: Visitors enter from three axes; flat sign rotates unsuccessfully; text ring unfolds; matching route symbols illuminate at each entrance.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A shared space may need more than one intended viewpoint.
premises.gate: Stylized station and gravity rules; not actual spacecraft signage, human-factors, or microgravity guidance.

premises.title: The Wish That Needed a Verb
premises.premise: A figure receives one wish token and asks for BETTER, causing a magical helper to improve random nearby objects while missing the real need. The figure replaces the vague word with HELP ME REACH THAT SHELF, and the helper grows one small stable-looking fantasy step so the figure can retrieve a cherished drawing.
premises.hook: Better what? The wish is improvising.
premises.visible_action: Objects gain absurd sparkles and extra drawers; wish text changes into a concrete request; one step appears; drawing is reached.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A concrete goal is easier to act on than a vague improvement.
premises.gate: Fictional wish logic and magical step; not practical climbing or assistive-device advice.

premises.title: The Sign at Knee Height
premises.premise: A park volunteer wants all visitors to find a small puppet show, but the only direction sign is hidden behind a crowd’s shoulders. They add a second matching sign on a clear low stand and a visible path symbol, allowing both tall and short cartoon visitors to follow the same route.
premises.hook: The directions disappear when everyone arrives.
premises.visible_action: Crowd gathers; overhead sightline blocks; low sign slides into open view; matching ground symbols lead to the puppet stage.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Check an instruction from more than one viewpoint.
premises.gate: Do not claim accessibility compliance from a cartoon; real public signage requires relevant standards and user testing.

premises.title: The Shared Tool’s Return Ticket
premises.premise: A community craft table wants to keep one hole punch available, but it vanishes under half-finished paper projects. A volunteer adds a bright outline where it belongs and a removable BORROWED card carried with it; the next borrower finds the card, waits visibly, and receives the returned tool without a search.
premises.hook: The shared tool has entered the paper jungle.
premises.visible_action: Paper piles spread; tool outline is drawn; BORROWED card travels with the punch; tool returns to its marked spot and card flips.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: Make shared-resource status easy to see.
premises.gate: Use a blunt toy craft tool; no assertion that this prevents theft or meets workplace safety requirements.

premises.title: The Bench With Room for the Bag
premises.premise: A traveler wants to rest at a crowded toy bus stop, but bags occupy the remaining seats. A waiting passenger notices, moves their own bag to a designated shelf, and others copy the gesture, revealing one free seat without anyone delivering a lecture.
premises.hook: One small move makes a seat.
premises.visible_action: Bags sit like silent passengers; one bag rises to a shelf; others follow; traveler sits; everyone resumes waiting.
premises.intended_takeaway_or_theme: A small voluntary adjustment can open shared space.
premises.gate: Use an invented stop and designated bag shelf; do not infer strangers’ needs or instruct obstruction of real walkways.

premises.title: The Library Book That Came With a Map
premises.premise: A volunteer wants to return scattered toy library books to the correct shelves, but abstract section labels confuse every helper. They draw a simple shelf map using the same symbols as the spines, place it on the cart, and finish the return route with a new helper confidently leading.
premises.hook: The books know their symbols. The shelves need to match.
premises.visible_action: Cart stops between shelves; spine symbols compare; matching shelf map unfolds; books move into corresponding bays; helper takes the front handle.

premises.gate: Toy-scale staging only; real street closures, crowd routing, and accessibility require authorized planning and applicable standards.
